title: Getting started
summary: Complete setup checklist for new CareStream accounts
text: Follow these steps to get CareStream working for your team. Each step unlocks more of the platform. Upload your policies. Go to Policies in the sidebar and upload your policy documents (PDF or Word). CareStream reads these to answer staff questions. Add your staff. Go to Staff and add each team member with their name, email address, and role. This lets CareStream personalise responses and track training progress. Configure your settings. Go to Settings and set up your dedicated email address (for email queries), configure any access restrictions you need, and set your AI sign-off message — the line every answer ends with (e.g. “The Crossways Care Team”). Until you set it, answers sign off as “The CareStream Team”. Tell your team. Share the portal link or email address with your staff so they can start asking questions. Upload your CQC report. Go to Policies , select category CQC Report , and upload your most recent inspection report. This enables the CQC Report Chat feature. You can complete steps 1 to 3 in any order, but you must add at least one policy document before staff can use the Chat Hub.

title: Uploading policies & documents
summary: How to add, update and categorise your policy documents, including duplicate detection when the same policy is uploaded under a different name

blocks.title: What to upload
blocks.text: Upload any document your staff might need to reference: care policies, staff handbooks, risk assessments, procedures, or your CQC report. Supported formats are PDF and Word (.docx).

blocks.title: How to upload
blocks.text: Go to Policies in the left sidebar. Click Upload document and select your file. Choose the correct category. This controls which AI pipeline is used to answer questions about it. Wait for the status to show Indexed . This usually takes 30 to 60 seconds depending on file size.

blocks.title: Document categories
blocks.text: Policies & Procedures Your internal care setting policies, SOPs, and risk assessments Staff Handbook Employee handbook, HR policies, and onboarding documents External Regulation Legislation or external guidance (e.g. CQC Key Questions) Training Module Training materials and learning resources for staff CQC Report Your most recent CQC inspection report. Enables CQC Report Chat.

blocks.title: Policy sections (internal policies)
blocks.text: Internal policies can be filed under a section : e.g. Safeguarding, GDPR, Infection control, so your library is organised and easy to scan. Each section shows in its own colour in a dedicated column on the Policies page. When you upload internal policies, choose the Section shown next to the category. For a bulk upload it applies to the whole batch, so upload each section's policies together. To add your own sections, go to Settings → Policy sections , type a name and click Add . Remove one with the × on its chip. Any section you add appears in the dropdown the next time you upload, and gets its own colour automatically. You start with 15 standard sections (Activities, Admission management, Safeguarding, Training, and more). Add as many of your own as you need to match how your policies are grouped.

blocks.title: Duplicate detection
blocks.text: When you upload a policy, CareStream checks it against your existing library so you don't end up with the same policy twice. It looks at two things: The file & name , at the point of upload: an identical file, or one with the same name as an existing policy, is caught straight away and you're offered Replace or Keep both. The actual content , once the policy has processed: CareStream compares the text of the new policy against your other policies. So if the same policy is uploaded under a different name (for example “Holiday Policy” and “Staff Annual Leave Policy”), it's still recognised as a likely duplicate even though the names differ. When a content match is found, a “looks like a duplicate” panel appears at the top of your Policies page, showing the match percentage and what it matched. You choose: Replace — the new upload takes over and the existing policy is archived. Keep both — they're genuinely different; save them side by side. Discard this upload — the new one was a mistake; archive it and keep the existing policy. Nothing is deleted automatically, CareStream only flags a possible match and leaves the decision to you. The reverse also happens: if a new policy has a similar name to one you already have but the content is actually different (for example a “Staff Alcohol Policy” and an “Alcohol & Drug Use” policy), CareStream shows a short “checked, kept as separate policies” note with the content match score, so you can see we compared them properly and that they're genuinely different documents, both worth keeping.

blocks.title: Preview how a policy reads for staff
blocks.text: Click Preview on any active policy to see it exactly as your staff do when they open the full copy or read it in their induction, with the letterhead, address, phone/email and footers removed and the text tidied into clean, readable sections. There's a toggle to switch between “As staff see it” and the “Original text” , so you can check nothing important was stripped. It's a quick way to make sure a policy looks right before your team relies on it.

title: Managing staff
summary: Adding team members, CSV bulk import, roles, and access controls

blocks.title: Adding staff members
blocks.text: Go to Staff in the sidebar and click Add staff member ; enter their name and email address. Choose their Position from the dropdown (Care Assistant, Nurse, Chef, etc.). This is the key field, it decides which onboarding and training they receive. If they hold a specialist role (e.g. Infection Control, Night Staff), answer Yes and pick one or more from the list. These add extra, specialist onboarding and training on top of their position. Choose the Staff type : New starter auto-enrols them in the onboarding for their position and specialisms; Existing staff member doesn't. Optionally set their first/second language, then share the login details shown on screen. Right after creating a staff member you're offered a quick Assign training step, tick the modules that apply (statutory ones are pre-selected). You can always do this later from their detail card too.

blocks.title: Import your whole team from a spreadsheet (CSV)
blocks.text: Setting up a new home? Instead of adding people one at a time, click Import from CSV next to the Add staff member button and upload a staff list exported from your rota, HR or payroll system (Excel and Google Sheets both save as CSV). There is a blank template to download if you would rather start from scratch. Upload your CSV. Each person needs a name and an email address; job role, phone number, shift and first language are picked up too when your file has them. Match your columns. CareStream matches your spreadsheet headings to its fields automatically, check the matches and correct any, and set anything your file does not have to “Not in my file”. Check the details. Rows missing something are highlighted, type the missing details straight into the row, or untick it to leave that person out and add them individually later. UK mobile numbers are tidied up automatically, and duplicates are unticked for you. Import. Before you press Import, choose the staff type for the file: New starters are automatically enrolled in the onboarding flows matching their job roles, Existing staff members are not. Accounts are then created one by one; when it finishes you see every temporary password once, can download them all as a CSV, and can optionally have each person emailed their own login automatically. Assign training. On the completion screen, click Assign training to all to give every imported person the same training in one go, statutory modules are pre-selected, just as when you add someone individually. You can fine-tune individuals from their staff record afterwards. (Training-only accounts allocate their purchased licences from the Training page instead.) The import creates accounts exactly as the Add staff member form does, so plan staff limits apply and each person appears on the Staff page immediately with their onboarding and training already in place.

blocks.title: Viewing & managing a staff member
blocks.text: Click a staff member's name on the Staff page to open their detail card, a single view of everything they're set up for: Their profile : position, specialist roles, shift, email access and account status. Language : their first and second language, and the communication toggle (below). Training : every module assigned to them with a live status (Not started, In progress, Complete, Expired). Use + Assign training to add more at any time. Onboarding : the induction flows they're enrolled on, with step-by-step progress. Use + Assign onboarding to enrol them on more (flows they're already on are marked and can't be double-assigned). To change their details (name, position, specialisms, languages or shift) use Edit details on the card (or the ⋮ menu on their row).

blocks.title: Getting staff into the hub (no password)
blocks.text: The easiest way to get a care assistant signed in on their phone is a passwordless sign-in link : no password to type or remember. On a staff member's detail card, click Sign-in link . You'll get a QR code they can scan, a link you can copy , or an Email it to them button. It works once and lasts 14 days; signing in this way also keeps them logged in on that phone for a long time. To invite many staff at once (for example right after a CSV import), click Hub invites at the top of the Staff page. Pick who to invite (people who have never signed in are ticked for you), then either email everyone their own sign-in link in one go, or print a QR sheet with a personal code per person for the staff room. Each code signs its owner straight in, works once, and lasts 14 days. Staff can also get themselves in: on the sign-in page there's an “Email me a sign-in link” option, so they never need to remember a password. Once they're in, encourage them to add CareStream to their home screen and turn on notifications (see the Chat Hub guide), that's how the hub keeps staff nudged.

blocks.title: Positions & specialist roles — how they drive onboarding & training
blocks.text: A staff member's position is the single most important thing you set, because CareStream uses it to give them the right onboarding and the right training questions for their job, a Care Assistant's induction and quizzes are different from a Nurse's or a Chef's. Specialist roles work on top of the position. If someone is a Senior Care Assistant who is also your Infection Control lead, they get the Senior Care Assistant onboarding plus the Infection Control specialist onboarding, and their training is tailored to both. Both lists are managed in Settings → Positions and Settings → Specialist roles . The standard care/nursing positions and specialisms are already there; add any extras specific to your home and they'll appear in the dropdowns straight away. You can also add one without leaving the staff form : in the Position or Specialist role dropdown (when adding or editing a staff member) choose “＋ Add a new position” (or “＋ Add a new specialist role” ), type the new one and click Add . It's selected for that staff member and saved to your Settings list, so it's available for everyone from then on, no need to go to Settings first.

blocks.title: Language preferences
blocks.text: When adding a staff member you can record their first language and an optional second language . CareStream uses the first language to send training questions and automated messages in the staff member's own language, if their first language is Polish, their training quiz questions arrive in Polish. The same applies to renewal reminders and other proactive communications. Each staff member has an “Always communicate in their first language” toggle (in the Add / Edit forms and on their detail card). When it's on : the default, every message CareStream sends them is translated into their first language. Turn it off for staff who'd rather receive everything in English. You can flip it instantly from the detail card. Over 180 languages are supported. If your team speaks one that isn't already listed, you don't have to leave the form: click “Language not listed? Add it” beneath the first or second language dropdown and start typing the language's English name. Matching languages appear as you type, so pick one from the list to avoid misspellings (e.g. start typing “Sho” and choose “Shona”). If it isn't in our catalogue, type the full name and press Add . Either way it's saved to your account, selected on the form, and appears in the first & second language dropdowns from then on. You can also add or remove languages any time in Settings → Languages . A note on translation quality CareStream translates content into a staff member's language on demand, so it isn't limited to a fixed list, you can add almost any language. Quality does vary by how widely a language is written online: Excellent for the languages most of your team are likely to speak, for example Polish, Romanian, Portuguese, Spanish, Arabic, Urdu, Hindi and the major Indian languages, Tagalog, Swahili, Yoruba, Somali, Amharic and all European languages. Good for most other widely spoken languages, such as Shona, Twi, Igbo, Nepali and Sinhala. Best effort for very small or rarely written languages. Here the translation may be partial, and if it can't be produced reliably CareStream falls back to clear English rather than showing anything incorrect, so a staff member is never left with a broken screen. In short: adding a language always makes it selectable, and for the languages your workforce actually speaks the translation is dependable. To get the best results, set the staff member's first language to the one they read most comfortably, and keep the “always communicate in their first language” toggle on. Translation glossary (term-locking). You can make translations more consistent by pinning important terms in Settings → Translation glossary . Add words that should never be translated, your care setting's name, staff names, medication names, systems like “CQC” or “eMAR”, and role titles, so they stay in English in every language. You can also add a short note explaining what a term means (for example “eMAR” = “electronic Medication Administration Record”) so it's translated correctly every time. The glossary applies everywhere CareStream translates, training questions, annual modules, inductions, CQC prep, policies and staff messages, and takes effect straight away. You'll also see a set of Saved terms at the top of the glossary, common sector words like CQC, DoLS, eMAR and NMC that CareStream maintains for every care setting. They're applied automatically; if one doesn't suit your care setting you can Remove it (and add it back any time), and your own entry for a term always takes priority. Staff-improved translations (Translation Review). Beyond the glossary, you can let a trusted bilingual team member improve translations directly. Turn on “Let them suggest better translations” on a staff member's Edit screen (it's off for everyone by default). They then see a “Suggest a better translation” option on translated training, lessons, induction and CQC prep in their hub. Their suggestions come to you under Translation Review (in the sidebar), where you Approve , Edit or Reject each one. An approved suggestion replaces the machine translation of that exact phrase, in that language, for your care setting, everywhere it appears. Approval is required by default; you can switch on Auto-approve in Translation Review to let your permitted staff's suggestions go live immediately. Over time this builds a library of human-checked translations, useful evidence that staff can understand their training.

blocks.title: Letting staff switch a set into their second language
blocks.text: Some staff have good English but a different native tongue. The idea is that everyone learns in English, but when a particular set is hard to follow they can read just that one in their own language. To allow this, set the staff member up with a first language of English and their native tongue as the second language , then turn on “Allow switching a set to their second language” (in the Add / Edit forms and on their detail card, just below the communication toggle). Hover the i next to it for a reminder of what it does. With it on, that staff member sees a small language button on each individual set in their hub, across My Training , Annual Training , Induction , Follow-up and CQC Prep . Tapping it flips just that one set (the lesson, the questions and the multiple-choice answers) into their second language so they can understand it. The button then reads “1st language” so they can flip straight back. The switch is session only : nothing is remembered, so every visit starts in their first language. It only changes what they read, their answers, scores and progress are unaffected. The toggle stays hidden unless the staff member has a second language set. Every time a staff member flips a set, CareStream records it so you can see where the language and training gaps are. The team-wide picture is on Analytics → Overview (“Second-language switching”) and the per-staff breakdown is on Analytics → Staff . If you see the same set switched often, it is a good prompt to offer extra support or simplify the wording.

blocks.title: Improving translations: glossary & staff review
blocks.text: CareStream translates training, lessons, induction, CQC prep and messages into each staff member's language automatically. Two tools let you make those translations more accurate for your care setting, and they work together. 1. Translation glossary (pin the right words) In Settings → Translation glossary you pin terms so they're always handled your way, either kept in English (your care setting's name, staff names, medication names, systems like CQC or eMAR, role titles) or with a short note explaining what a term means. The Saved terms at the top are common sector words CareStream maintains for every care setting (CQC, DoLS, eMAR, NMC and so on); you can Remove any that don't suit you and add them back later. Your own entry for a term always wins. 2. Staff-verified translations (Translation Review) The glossary fixes individual words; this fixes whole phrases. A trusted bilingual team member can propose better wording directly, and you approve it. Here's the flow: Grant permission. On a staff member's Edit screen (or their detail card when you click their name), turn on “Let them suggest better translations” . It's off for everyone by default, so only the people you choose can suggest. They suggest. When that person views content in their own language , they can improve it in two ways. On questions and answers (training, induction, CQC prep) a small “Suggest a better translation” link opens the wording to edit. On lesson text , they simply click the paragraph or heading (a small pencil appears on hover), fix it in place and send. This also works when a staff member reads a set in their second language via the language button. You review. Suggestions arrive under Translation Review in the sidebar (with a count on the Pending tab). Each shows the English source, the current machine translation and the staff member's version side by side. You can Approve , Edit & approve , or Reject . It goes live. Once approved, that wording replaces the machine translation for that exact phrase, in that language, for your care setting, everywhere it appears, instantly and permanently. Approval is required by default , so nothing your staff suggest changes what others see until you've checked it. If you'd rather your permitted staff's suggestions go live immediately, turn on Auto-approve at the top of Translation Review. Rejecting a suggestion simply keeps the machine translation. Over time this builds a library of human-checked translations, useful evidence for inspection that staff can understand their training in their own language. Nothing here can make a translation worse: if a phrase has no approved wording, staff simply see the normal machine translation (which always falls back to clear English if a language can't be produced reliably).

blocks.title: Approved senders (added automatically)
blocks.text: When you add a staff member, their email address is automatically added to the Approved sender addresses list in Settings . You don't need to add them in two places. The list in Settings shows each entry alongside the staff member it belongs to, for example jane@example.com, Jane Smith (Care Assistant) , so you can see at a glance who each address belongs to. Only addresses on this list can query CareStream by email; messages from anyone else are ignored. You can still add shared or external addresses manually in Settings.

The button then reads “1st language” so they can flip straight back. The switch is session only : nothing is remembered, so every visit starts in their first language. It only changes what they read, their answers, scores and progress are unaffected. The toggle stays hidden unless the staff member has a second language set. Every time a staff member flips a set, CareStream records it so you can see where the language and training gaps are. The team-wide picture is on Analytics → Overview (“Second-language switching”) and the per-staff breakdown is on Analytics → Staff . If you see the same set switched often, it is a good prompt to offer extra support or simplify the wording. Improving translations: glossary & staff review CareStream translates training, lessons, induction, CQC prep and messages into each staff member's language automatically. Two tools let you make those translations more accurate for your care setting, and they work together. 1. Translation glossary (pin the right words) In Settings → Translation glossary you pin terms so they're always handled your way, either kept in English (your care setting's name, staff names, medication names, systems like CQC or eMAR, role titles) or with a short note explaining what a term means. The Saved terms at the top are common sector words CareStream maintains for every care setting (CQC, DoLS, eMAR, NMC and so on); you can Remove any that don't suit you and add them back later. Your own entry for a term always wins. 2. Staff-verified translations (Translation Review) The glossary fixes individual words; this fixes whole phrases. A trusted bilingual team member can propose better wording directly, and you approve it. Here's the flow: Grant permission. On a staff member's Edit screen (or their detail card when you click their name), turn on “Let them suggest better translations” . It's off for everyone by default, so only the people you choose can suggest. They suggest. When that person views content in their own language , they can improve it in two ways. On questions and answers (training, induction, CQC prep) a small “Suggest a better translation” link opens the wording to edit. On lesson text , they simply click the paragraph or heading (a small pencil appears on hover), fix it in place and send. This also works when a staff member reads a set in their second language via the language button. You review. Suggestions arrive under Translation Review in the sidebar (with a count on the Pending tab). Each shows the English source, the current machine translation and the staff member's version side by side. You can Approve , Edit & approve , or Reject . It goes live. Once approved, that wording replaces the machine translation for that exact phrase, in that language, for your care setting, everywhere it appears, instantly and permanently. Approval is required by default , so nothing your staff suggest changes what others see until you've checked it. If you'd rather your permitted staff's suggestions go live immediately, turn on Auto-approve at the top of Translation Review. Rejecting a suggestion simply keeps the machine translation. Over time this builds a library of human-checked translations, useful evidence for inspection that staff can understand their training in their own language. Nothing here can make a translation worse: if a phrase has no approved wording, staff simply see the normal machine translation (which always falls back to clear English if a language can't be produced reliably). Approved senders (added automatically) When you add a staff member, their email address is automatically added to the Approved sender addresses list in Settings . You don't need to add them in two places. The list in Settings shows each entry alongside the staff member it belongs to, for example jane@example.com, Jane Smith (Care Assistant) , so you can see at a glance who each address belongs to. Only addresses on this list can query CareStream by email; messages from anyone else are ignored. You can still add shared or external addresses manually in Settings. Adding a staff member creates a login for them. By default we also email them a one-time sign-in link (the Email them a sign-in link now box is ticked; untick it if you would rather pass the details on yourself). Importing from a spreadsheet does not send emails. You'll also see their credentials once, on screen, so you can share them securely. If they ever need to get back in, use Re-send login from their menu: it emails them a one-time sign-in link (no password needed) and leaves their password alone. If they have forgotten their password and you want to give them a new one, use Reset password instead: it changes the password straight away and shows you the new one, with an option to email it.

title: Staff records & analytics
summary: The individual staff record, attention flags, and how to read it

blocks.title: Opening a staff record
blocks.text: Every staff member has a full record page : a single view of what they've been assigned, what they've completed, how they're scoring, and how engaged they are. Open it two ways from the Staff page: Click the small chart icon next to a name to jump straight to their record. Or click the name to open the quick overlay (where you assign training/onboarding), then use View full record → . Every section of the record has an ⓘ icon, hover or tap it for a plain-English explanation of what you're looking at. The notes below are the same guidance in one place.

blocks.title: Reading the record
blocks.text: Completion rings : the share of assigned items finished: training modules, induction flows, and the average quiz score across completed modules. Aim for 100%; a low average score is an early sign someone may not have understood the material. Needs attention : a coloured banner listing anything outstanding (overdue or expired training, overdue/stalled induction, never logged in). Red = urgent. How they compare to the team : the teal bar is this person's figure; the dark tick is your home's average. A bar sitting left of the tick is below average and may be worth a conversation. Required training for their role : the training their job role must hold, with a status and dates for each course, a percentage in date, and their safe to work checks from the Workforce page. It uses the same rules as the Training Matrix tab, so the two always agree, and it is included in the CQC evidence PDF. Training record : every module with its status and score (the % of quiz questions answered correctly). "Expires" applies to annual modules due for renewal; "Overdue" means past the due date and not complete. Reset clears a module so they can retake it. Induction record : their onboarding flows, with a bar showing steps completed and an "X/Y correct" count for the question steps. Engagement : how actively they use CareStream: questions asked in the portal, the topics they ask about, CQC prep answered, and logins. Low engagement alongside overdue training is a useful early warning. Completions (6 months) & Activity timeline : momentum over time and a dated history of everything they've done. The timeline is good evidence of ongoing development.

blocks.title: Actions on the record
blocks.text: Send reminder : immediately sends the staff member their outstanding training questions by email (it doesn't wait for the scheduled send). CQC evidence (PDF) : downloads the whole record as a PDF: training matrix, scores, induction sign-off and dates. Hand this to an inspector as proof a staff member is trained and inducted. Reset (per module), clears someone's answers and completion so they can take a module again.

blocks.title: Spotting problems across the whole team
blocks.text: The Analytics page has a “Staff needing attention” panel at the top. It surfaces everyone with a flag, overdue or expired training, overdue/stalled induction, or never logged in, so you can triage without opening each record. Each card links straight to that person's record, and urgent cases are dotted red.

blocks.title: Policy reading engagement
blocks.text: When staff read policies during their induction, CareStream records how they read them. You can see this two ways: On the staff record : a Policy reading table per person: the time they spent on each policy, the furthest they scrolled, and a label, Thorough (scrolled to the end), Skimmed (marked read without scrolling far) or Partial . This is included in the CQC evidence PDF. On the Analytics page : a Policy reading engagement section with team-wide figures (sessions, average time, average scroll depth, and % who read to the end). This data is for managers only, staff don't see their own reading stats on My Progress.

blocks.title: Induction question performance
blocks.text: Induction flows include questions, and CareStream marks each answer automatically, multiple-choice is graded instantly, and written answers are checked by AI. (If someone gets a multiple-choice question wrong, they're asked to try again before the step completes.) You can see how staff are doing in two places: On the staff record : an Induction questions section listing every question that person has answered, with a ✓ or ✗, their answer, and the correct answer where they got it wrong. A quick way to spot exactly where an individual needs support. Included in the CQC evidence PDF. On the Analytics page : an Induction question performance section: the percentage answered correctly across the team, plus a “Most-missed induction questions” list that highlights the topics where knowledge is weakest, so you know what to reinforce in supervision or training. CQC Staff Prep : each staff record also has a CQC Staff Prep section showing every prep question that person was assigned, their AI score, and any improvement after reviewing the model answer and retrying. The team-wide view (including the review-and-retry improvement) is in Analytics → CQC Staff Prep . Both feed the CQC evidence PDF.

blocks.title: Second-language switching
blocks.text: If you let a staff member switch a set into their second language (see Managing staff → Language preferences ), CareStream records each time they do it, so you can see where the language and training gaps are. You can read this two ways: Analytics → Overview : a “Second-language switching” card with the team-wide picture, total switches, how many staff use it, a breakdown by language and by area, and the most switched sets. No individual names, this is the generalist view. Analytics → Staff : a per-staff breakdown showing exactly who switched, which sets they flipped, and how often. A set that is switched again and again is a good prompt to offer extra support or to simplify its wording.

blocks.text: Staff have their own read-only My Progress page in the portal (top menu and chat sidebar). It shows their completion rings, what's left to finish with quick links to do it, how they compare to the team, and their training & induction lists. If a staff member's “always communicate in their first language” setting is on, their entire My Progress page, including the ⓘ help bubbles, is shown in that language , so non-English speakers can follow their own progress without help.

title: Knowledge gaps & follow-up
summary: How wrong answers turn into reinforced learning, and how you track it

blocks.title: The idea
blocks.text: When a staff member gets a training or induction question wrong, that's a knowledge gap . Rather than letting it sit, CareStream turns it into a short piece of learning and then checks they've got it, so the gap actually closes. The whole loop is automatic; this section explains what your team sees and what you can track.

blocks.title: What staff see — “Follow-up” in the Chat Hub
blocks.text: Anyone with an unanswered or incorrectly-answered question gets a Follow-up item in their hub (with a red badge). Opening it, they choose: Learn & retry : a short, plain-language micro-lesson built from your own policies : why the right answer matters, the key points to remember, a real-life scenario to think through, an optional “ask about this policy” chat, and then a fresh question to confirm they've understood (never the identical one). Just retry : simply re-answer the original question. If they get it wrong, there's a nudge to learn the point instead. The lesson is shown in the staff member's first language if their “always communicate in first language” setting is on. Answering correctly clears the item from their Follow-up immediately. The micro-lessons are grounded only in your home's policies (and anonymised reference policies for general training topics), they won't invent rules. They're generated once and reused, so they appear quickly.

blocks.title: On the staff record — “How gaps get resolved”
blocks.text: Each person's record ( Staff → record ) shows two things about gaps: Recommended follow-up : the questions they currently have wrong, with actions to re-send the questions or mark the gap as reviewed (supervision evidence). How gaps get resolved : a count of Learn & retry vs Just retry , an “engaged with learning” percentage, and a recent list. A healthy lean towards Learn & retry means the person is genuinely engaging, not just clicking through. Both are included in the CQC evidence PDF.

blocks.title: Across the team — the “Knowledge gaps” analytics
blocks.text: The Analytics page has a Knowledge gaps section pulling training and induction together: Summary : open gaps, staff affected, gaps closed in the last 30 days, and the team's “engaged with learning” percentage. Most-missed questions & Weakest topics : exactly where to aim a refresher or supervision. Knowledge gaps over time : a trend chart showing whether open gaps are rising or falling (it builds up from a daily snapshot). How gaps are being closed : the team-wide Learn-vs-retry split and a recent feed.

blocks.title: Weekly digest & staff reminders
blocks.text: Every Monday , CareStream emails admins a knowledge-gap digest (open gaps with a week-on-week change, most-missed questions and weakest topics), and sends staff with open gaps a gentle reminder to complete their Follow-up. Both honour the Knowledge-gap digest switch in Settings → Email preferences : turn it off to stop all of it. Use Send digest now on the Analytics page to email yourself the current digest at any time (handy before a supervision or inspection).

title: Policy Gap Detection
summary: The guided four-step pipeline, regulation coverage, what to add, out-of-date content, cross-policy consistency, CQC wording, resumable runs, the policy update matrix, legal-change tracking, gap training, correcting typos and renaming policies yourself, and policy updates with admin, care manager and external approvals — Professional & Enterprise

blocks.title: The guided pipeline: run the four checks in order
blocks.text: The Gaps page is a guided pipeline of four numbered steps, and the order matters. Every analysis reads the published version of your policies, so if you adopt fixes but never publish them, the next run will report the same issues again. Regulation coverage : find missing and partial regulations, and adopt the suggested additions. Out-of-date content : scan for stale terminology and superseded guidance in what you now hold. Cross-policy consistency : check your policies against each other for contradictions. CQC wording alignment : polish the surviving text into the person-centred voice CQC looks for. Between steps, go to Policies , open Adopted changes to review , and approve and publish what you adopted. That one publish round between steps is the intended rhythm: run, adopt, publish, next step. The page keeps you on track with: Step status pills showing when each step last ran, with an (i) hover explaining the cycle. An amber “policies to publish” counter in the overview strip whenever adopted changes are waiting, which links straight to the Policies page. A pre-run check every time you press a run button: if changes are still unpublished it warns you the run will not see them, and offers to take you to Policies first. Stale flags when policies have been published or newly uploaded since a step last ran, a nudge that its results are now out of date. A publish reminder on the Policies page itself: after you publish, a banner suggests re-running your Gaps analyses so the results reflect the new version. Seeing the same findings after adopting fixes? That almost always means the changes are adopted but not yet published . Publish them on the Policies page, then re-run.

blocks.title: Interrupted runs resume where they stopped
blocks.text: The longer analyses (coverage, consistency and wording) work through your policies in small batches and save progress on our servers as they go . It is fastest to keep the page open while a run works, but if your connection drops, you close the tab or you are signed out mid-run, nothing is lost. When you come back, an amber Resume banner on the affected section shows how much was already done (for example “18 of 24 analysed”). Pressing Resume continues from where it stopped. Items already analysed are not re-processed and use no extra AI tokens . If a section ever fails to load you will see a clear “Couldn't load this section” message with a Retry button rather than an empty panel. Retrying is free, it simply reloads the saved results.

blocks.title: Regulation coverage, read from your policy content
blocks.text: Click Run coverage analysis (about a minute). For every regulation that applies to your service, CareStream searches the actual content of all your policies and an AI auditor judges whether you substantively cover it: Covered — a policy clearly addresses it (the policy is named). Partial — touched on but incomplete. Gap — not addressed anywhere in your policies. A regulation is only flagged when your documents genuinely don't cover it, never just because no policy is named after it. Re-run it whenever you upload or update policies. The coverage score is fully-covered regulations, plus partials at half weight, out of the total that apply to you.

blocks.title: What to add — and where
blocks.text: On any partial or gap, click See what to add / Show coverage & what to add . CareStream shows the specific requirements you're missing with example wording you can adapt , and — importantly — verifies each one against your whole library first, so it never tells you to add something you already hold in another policy. Where it goes : it names the existing policy to add the wording to, or tells you a new policy is needed. Legal basis : each item is marked Legally required or Advised good practice , naming the regulation and linking the source. Highlighting : on a partial, the “Where it's covered” tab opens the policy with the covered passages highlighted. The example wording is guidance for you to review, adapt and approve — not legal advice. Prefer it done for you? Use “Request this policy” and our team can write and supply it.

blocks.title: Three ways to deal with a suggestion
blocks.text: You are never forced to take a suggestion as written. Each one in the left-hand column offers three choices, and CareStream remembers what you decided — so re-running the analysis does not keep proposing something you have already dealt with. Adopt into [policy] : use the suggestion as intended. You can edit the wording first, and insert your own names and job titles from the chips underneath. On a replacement, it swaps the highlighted paragraph in full. Add as new section : for when the wording is good but the replacement does not work for you. Instead of changing your existing paragraph, the wording is added as a new section at the bottom of the policy , under a heading CareStream suggests and you can edit. Your original wording is left exactly as it is. Ignore : you do not want it. The suggestion turns grey and will not be raised again on future runs. Both Add as new section and Ignore can be reversed at any time — a decided suggestion shows an Undo button, and undoing puts it straight back into your outstanding list. Decisions are per policy : ignoring a requirement on one policy does not silence the same requirement if a later analysis routes it to a different policy. A new section still goes through review : like any adopted change it lands in Adopted changes to review on the Policies page, and only appears in the policy once you approve and publish it. Where it sits : a new section is placed at the end of the policy, above the review dates and sign-off, so the document still closes properly. Use Add as new section when your existing paragraph is worded the way your service actually works and you do not want it rewritten — you keep your wording and still evidence the requirement. Use Ignore when the requirement genuinely does not apply to your service, so your outstanding list reflects real work rather than noise.

blocks.title: Fixing typos and missing words yourself
blocks.text: Gap detection finds what is missing against the regulations. It will not flag a spelling mistake or a dropped word, because nothing is legally absent — but those are exactly the things you notice while reading a policy properly. You can now correct them yourself, without re-uploading the document. Hover any line of the policy — a paragraph, a heading or a bullet. It tints, and a small pencil appears beside it. Click it to open that line for editing, with spellcheck on. Fix the word. Save the correction. Press Save correction , or Ctrl/Cmd + Enter. Press Escape to cancel. This works in two places : in the policy shown beside a gap on the Gaps page, and on the Policies page when you open Policy preview . Only administrators can do it — staff reading policies in the hub, and anyone reviewing one through an external review link, see the policy exactly as it is. No approval needed, and it is live straight away : a wording correction is not a policy change, so it does not go to your care manager or external reviewer. It updates the version staff read immediately and takes a point version — 3.0 becomes 3.1. Staff keep their acknowledgements : nobody is asked to re-read a policy because a typo was fixed. It is still recorded : every correction is kept with who made it and when, sits in the policy's version history, and can be undone like any other change. Changes waiting for approval are untouched : if you have adopted gap fixes that have not been published yet, correcting a typo does not push them live early. Two things you may see. If a paragraph already has a suggested change attached to it, you get a short warning — rewording it can stop that suggestion fitting, so adopt the suggestion first where you can. And the editor sometimes opens showing slightly different spacing from the text above it: the preview tidies the document for reading, while the editor shows the wording as it is actually stored. That stored wording is the one worth correcting. You cannot edit a suggestion that has not been adopted yet — that wording is not in your policy until you adopt it, so there is nothing to correct. Adopt it first, publish, then fix any wording you want to change.

blocks.title: Renaming a policy
blocks.text: On the Policies page, hover a policy in the list and a pencil appears next to its name. Click it, type the new name, then press Enter to save or Escape to cancel. Uploaded documents are often named after the file they came from, so this is the quickest way to make your list read the way your service actually refers to its policies. Renaming changes the display name only — the document, its content, its version history and its approvals are all untouched, and nothing needs re-analysing. The new name is used everywhere the policy is referred to, including gap suggestions and staff search, and the change is recorded with the previous name.

blocks.title: CQC wording alignment (Single Assessment Framework)
blocks.text: Covering the rules is one thing; reading the way CQC expects is another. Alongside what's missing, CareStream checks whether a policy is written the person-centred, outcomes-focused way the CQC Single Assessment Framework looks for, not just whether it is procedurally correct. In the Coverage detail for a regulation, a CQC wording alignment section runs automatically for the policy shown. What it flags : where a policy covers the requirement but reads too procedurally, it suggests a person-centred alternative in your policy's own voice . Where it goes : each suggestion is numbered (W1, W2…) and highlighted on the policy on the right, so you can see exactly where it belongs. Adopt it : accept a suggestion and it becomes a tracked change, going through the same review and approval as any other policy update. In CQC's language : it names the quality statement the policy supports, so you can speak to it directly at inspection. Because it is about how the policy reads , the check only runs where a policy already exists for the regulation. The suggestions are yours to review, adapt and approve.

blocks.title: Out-of-date content — superseded law, regulators and placeholders
blocks.text: Policies drift out of date. On the Gaps page, under Regulation coverage , the Out-of-date content section scans every policy for wording that has been superseded — old legislation and regulators (for example the Data Protection Act 1998, CRB checks, CSCI, or Primary Care Trusts), pandemic-era guidance, and unfilled template placeholders. Click Scan policies to run it; it's instant. A clear list : each flagged policy shows how many issues were found, so you can see at a glance which ones need attention. Review & fix : open a policy and the out-of-date wording is highlighted in place. Show in policy jumps you to each occurrence, one click at a time. One-click replace : swap the outdated wording for the current term (for example CRB → DBS, or KLOEs → Single Assessment Framework) everywhere it appears in the policy. Same approval as any update : a replacement becomes a tracked change on your policy draft and goes through the same review and approval before it's published — nothing changes automatically. Re-scan whenever you upload or update policies. The suggestions are yours to review and approve; replacements are applied to your draft, not published for you.

blocks.title: Cross-policy consistency — policies that contradict each other
blocks.text: Coverage and out-of-date checks look at one policy at a time. Cross-policy consistency looks between policies — it finds where two of your policies say different, incompatible things about the same point : conflicting timeframes, escalation routes, named responsibilities or definitions, and drift between near-duplicate policies (two versions of the same policy that have quietly grown apart). Find it on the Gaps page under Cross-policy consistency , and press Run consistency check . It compares the right policies : it groups policies that cover the same subject, and policies that are near-duplicates of each other, so it only compares ones that could genuinely conflict — not every policy against every other. It only flags real contradictions : a genuine clash on the same point, not a difference of wording or a policy simply saying more than another. Review side by side : open a conflict to see each policy's wording, switch between the policies with the disputed passage highlighted, and pick which one is correct . Align in one click : once you've chosen the correct value, align the other policies to it — each change goes through the same review and approval as any other policy update. Dismiss false alarms : if two statements are actually compatible in context, dismiss the conflict and it won't return on the next check. Because it reads your policies with AI, it runs only when you press Run consistency check (not automatically). Re-run it after you've made significant changes to your library.

blocks.title: Policy update matrix — what changed, and when it's next due
blocks.text: Every time you adopt and publish a change, the policy is recorded in the Policy update matrix at the bottom of the Gaps page. It is your at-a-glance record of what has been kept up to date and what is coming up for review — useful for your own tracking and to show an inspector a maintained library. What drove the update : each policy is tagged with where the change came from — Regulation coverage , Out-of-date content , or Cross-policy consistency . Completed date : when the updated version went live to your staff. Next review date, set automatically : publishing counts as a review, so the policy's next review is set to 12 months from that date. Anything past due is flagged. The matrix fills in as you publish updates, so the more you keep on top of gaps and out-of-date content, the fuller your maintained-library record becomes.

blocks.title: A one-time disclaimer before you use the guidance
blocks.text: The first time anyone at your service opens the “what to add” guidance, CareStream shows a short legal disclaimer that must be accepted before the recommendations are shown. It makes clear that the gaps and example wording are guidance, not legal or compliance advice , that you remain responsible for reviewing and approving any changes, and that we strongly recommend any changes you make are checked by a suitably qualified external specialist before they are adopted . Shown once — after it's accepted, you won't see it again (unless the wording is materially updated). Required — if it isn't accepted, the “what to add” guidance stays locked; you can still see your coverage scores and gaps. Recorded — we keep a durable record of the acceptance (who accepted it, the date, and the version) as evidence. This protects you as much as us: it's a prompt to get a specialist eye on anything significant before you adopt it.

blocks.title: Only what applies to your service
blocks.text: We never flag regulations that don't apply to you. In Settings → Service profile , confirm a few facts about your service (do you cook on site, administer medicines, employ nurses, use hoists, support people under the Mental Health Act, and so on). These are pre-filled from your facility type — just check them. A home that holds no controlled drugs is never assessed against controlled-drug rules; a service that doesn't support people under the Mental Health Act is never flagged for it. blocks.title: When the rules change, you'll know
blocks.text: CareStream tracks changes to the standards you're assessed against. When one changes, a banner appears at the top of your Gaps page listing the affected regulations, so you can review your policies and re-run the analysis before it becomes an inspection finding. Dismiss any you've dealt with.

blocks.title: Turn a change into staff onboarding
blocks.text: Once you've added the recommended wording to a policy, click Generate onboarding . CareStream creates a read-and-confirm onboarding flow for that policy, so staff read (and acknowledge) the updated version. blocks.title: Getting an updated policy approved
blocks.text: Approvals run in stages that you control. An admin always approves first . From there the update can go to your care manager, then to an external person, before it is published to staff. If external approval is on, a one-off link is emailed to the person you choose. They read the policy and approve it or send it back with feedback. Every admin on the account receives them, and they come from “CareStream Policies” . Ready to send for external approval. Approved and published. When the external approver approves, your admins are emailed that the policy is now live for staff, with the new version number. Sent back by your external reviewer. blocks.title: The two approval switches
blocks.text: You set the workflow under Settings → Organisation details , in the “Policy approvals” panel. Require care manager approval (on by default). When on, an admin's approval sends the update to your care manager for a second approval. title: Policies we write for you
summary: When your policies are read against the law and a regulation has no policy behind it at all, we can write that policy for your home. How one is identified, written, delivered and approved, and where it sits in your own sign-off process.

blocks.title: 1. How a missing policy is identified
blocks.text: We hold the regulations, standards and guidance that apply to adult social care, and we work out which of them apply to your service rather than to care homes in general. A nursing home is asked different questions from a supported living service. Your policies are then read, properly read, not matched on their titles. That distinction matters. A policy called “Medical Gases” is about oxygen cylinders, not about the gas supply to your building, and a system that matched names would tick the wrong box and leave you exposed. We look at what each document is actually about. A policy is only reported as missing when nothing in your library covers that regulation's subject. If the analysis is out of date, or has never run, you are told that instead. We would rather say nothing than sell you something on a stale answer. The list names the regulations behind each policy. That is the answer to “why do we need this?” and it is worth reading before you decide.

blocks.title: 2. Ordering one
blocks.text: Missing policies appear on your Gaps page, below the four analysis steps, and in your suggestions. Tick the ones you want and order them. Payment is taken on a secure Stripe page; card details never touch CareStream. An invoice is raised and appears on your Billing page with the rest.

blocks.title: 3. How it is written
blocks.text: Each policy is written for your home, not adapted from a template. It is built around what the regulation actually requires, section by section, so that when you next run your gap analysis the policy answers it. It uses your home's name and the role holders you have named in Settings → Organisation details . Where you have not named someone, the policy names the role and leaves it at that. It never invents a person, a date, a contractor or a certificate number, and it never leaves a placeholder like “[name]” in your document. Name someone later and they appear automatically, with no rewrite. Filling in Organisation details before you order gives you a better document. The roles your policies actually mention are listed there, so you can see which are worth completing.

blocks.title: 4. We read it before you see it
blocks.text: Nothing reaches you the moment it is written. A person at CareStream reads every policy first and approves it. A document that carries your home's name should be seen by someone before it carries it.

blocks.title: 5. Then it enters your approval process, not ours
blocks.text: This is the part worth understanding. When we approve a policy, it is delivered . That is not the same as live . A delivered policy goes into exactly the same sign-off process as any other change to your policies, and your own settings decide what happens next. Require care manager approval is on : the policy waits in your care manager's Policies hub for their approval before it goes live. Require external approval is on : once the internal approvals are in, it goes out on a one-off link to your consultant or trustee. It is live only once they approve. Both off : it is published straight away, and still appears in your care manager's hub so they can see what arrived. You set both in Settings → Organisation details . We do not override them, and we cannot: a policy we wrote goes through your process the same as one you edited yourself.

blocks.title: 6. Afterwards
blocks.text: The policy sits in your library like any other, marked with a small CareStream badge so its origin is never in doubt, and it is indexed so your staff can ask questions about it. Re-run your regulation coverage and the gap it was written to close will close. From then on it is yours. Edit it, review it and version it exactly as you would a policy you wrote.

title: Staff onboarding flows
summary: Guided inductions for new starters, assigned automatically

blocks.title: What an onboarding flow is
blocks.text: An onboarding flow is a guided induction for new staff, an ordered checklist of steps they work through when they join. Each step is either a policy to read (so they confirm they've seen a key document) or a question to answer . New starters complete their flow from the staff portal, and you can track who has finished. There are three ways to get a flow: CareStream ready-made role flows (teal) — full inductions for common roles, mapped to your own policies when you adopt them. Generic onboarding policies (amber) — one of your own policies flagged for onboarding, added as a one-step read-and-confirm flow. Build your own — a flow you create from scratch with read and question steps. The sections below cover each, and the “Not ready” state that stops you enrolling staff on a flow that still has an unlinked read step.

blocks.title: Ready-made flows (the quickest way to start)
blocks.text: On the Onboarding page you'll see a set of ready-made flows built by CareStream for common care-home roles and specialisms. Click Adopt and CareStream: copies the flow into your own editable copy; automatically matches each step to your own uploaded policies (so “read the infection control policy” links to your infection control policy); and tailors the questions to the wording of your policies. If a step can't be matched (because you haven't uploaded a policy for that area yet), the flow tells you so you can upload it and link the step. You can edit anything afterwards. A flow with any unmatched read policy step is marked “Not ready” and you can't enrol staff on it until those steps are linked to a policy, so nobody is ever sent an induction with nothing to read. If you haven't uploaded any policies yet, upload them first: the ready-made flows read your policies.

blocks.title: Where the ready-made flows come from
blocks.text: The ready-made flows are built from a library of real care-sector policies that have been anonymised : every home name, address, person and contact detail removed, so they reflect genuine, well-written procedures without belonging to any one home. When you adopt a flow, CareStream uses this as the starting point but always matches and tailors it to your own policies, so what your staff read and answer is specific to your home.

blocks.title: Generic onboarding policies (turn any policy into a one-step flow)
blocks.text: Sometimes you just want new staff to read and confirm a specific policy as part of induction, without building a whole flow. Any of your own policies can be turned into a one-step onboarding flow. Flag the policy as a generic onboarding policy. When you upload a policy, set Generic Onboarding policy to Yes . For a policy already in your library, open the ⋯ menu on the Policies page and choose Use as onboarding policy (a small amber Onboarding tag then shows on it). You can remove it the same way. Go to Onboarding → Ready-made flows . Flagged policies appear in their own amber “Generic onboarding policies” section, separate from the CareStream role templates. Click Add as onboarding flow to create a one-step “read & confirm this policy” flow. It moves to Active flows , where you Enrol staff exactly like any other flow. Reading time and completion are tracked and count towards your CQC evidence. These are ideal for one-off must-reads (a new fire procedure, an updated visiting policy) that every staff member should acknowledge, without the overhead of a full role induction.

blocks.title: Multiple-choice questions
blocks.text: Questions can be multiple choice : staff pick an answer in the portal and it's marked instantly. A wrong answer asks them to review the policy and try again, so a completed flow is real evidence they understood it. You can also use free-text questions (CareStream assesses the answer) when you build your own steps.

blocks.title: Building your own flow
blocks.text: Click New flow , name it, and choose which job roles it applies to (leave blank for all staff). Add steps, a policy to read, or a question. When you add a read policy step, start typing the policy name and pick it from the list of your uploaded policies. For a question, fill all four options for an auto-marked multiple-choice question, or leave them blank for a free-text answer. Make sure the flow is active : only active flows are assigned to new starters. Flows you build yourself are marked Custom with a violet outline in Active flows , so you can tell them apart from CareStream ready-made flows and generic policy flows at a glance.

blocks.title: Generate questions from a policy with AI
blocks.text: When you build your own flow, CareStream can write the knowledge check questions for you, based on your own policy. This saves drafting multiple-choice questions by hand and keeps them faithful to what your policy actually says. Add a Read policy step and link it to a policy (start typing the policy name and choose it from the list). At the bottom of the steps, use the Generate questions from policy panel. Choose how many questions you want (1 to 5), and if your flow links more than one policy, pick which policy to use. Click Generate with AI . CareStream reads the linked policy and adds multiple-choice question steps, each with four options and the correct answer marked. Review and edit before saving. To try a different set, use Re-generate with AI , which replaces all the question steps in one go. A policy needs to have finished processing before you can generate from it. If it's still being read in, CareStream asks you to try again shortly. No policy linked yet? The panel reminds you to add a Read policy step and link a policy first, that policy is what the questions are drawn from.

blocks.title: Preview a flow & tidy up questions
blocks.text: On any flow in Active flows , click Preview to see the whole flow exactly as your staff work through it, each policy to read and each question with its answers (the correct one highlighted). It's the quickest way to sense-check a flow before you enrol anyone. Under every question you'll see its source , which depends on the type of flow: Ready-made role flows (adopted from CareStream) show “CareStream Sources” . We write and generate those questions for you in our own system, so they use none of your AI tokens. The 'read policy' steps in these flows are still matched to your policies. Flows you build yourself show your own policy for each question (for example “Generated from Infection Control Policy”), because those questions are drawn from the policy you chose. A question you typed by hand, or an older one, shows “Source not recorded”. This makes it easy to see where each question came from and to spot one that isn't relevant to the role or your policies. If a question or a policy step doesn't belong, click the × on it in the Preview and confirm, it's removed from the flow straight away, no need to open the full editor. For bigger changes (rewording a question, adding steps, changing answers), use Edit .

blocks.title: Tell us if a ready-made question isn't right (feedback loop)
blocks.text: The questions in ready-made role flows are written by CareStream (they show “CareStream Sources” in the Preview). To help us keep improving them, you can rate each one: in a ready-made flow's Preview , under each question you'll see “Is this question relevant to the role?” with a Yes and a No . Tap Yes if it's a good, relevant question. Tap No to tell us it's not relevant to the role or not a good question , and add an optional comment. Your feedback goes straight to the CareStream team. We review it to refine or replace weaker questions in the ready-made templates, so the inductions get more relevant for your roles over time. It doesn't change your flow immediately, if you want a question gone from your flow now, just delete it in the Preview as above.

blocks.title: Automatic enrolment for new starters
blocks.text: When you add a staff member and choose New starter , CareStream automatically enrols them in every active flow (adopted or your own) that matches their position or any of their specialist roles . So a new Nurse who is also Night Staff joins both the Nurse induction and the Night Staff specialist flow. Set the flows up once and every new starter is enrolled from day one, the confirmation screen tells you how many they joined.

blocks.title: Tracking progress
blocks.text: Each flow shows its enrolled staff and how far through they are, giving you a clear, auditable record that every new starter completed their induction, useful CQC evidence.

blocks.title: Reading policies during induction
blocks.text: When an induction step asks staff to read a policy, they tap Read policy to open the full document in a clean, readable view (letterhead and contact details are stripped out and it's laid out with headings and bullet points). If the staff member's first language is set and their communication toggle is on, the policy is shown in their language . They can also Save for later , which pins the policy to a Saved policies list in their Chat Hub sidebar. CareStream quietly records how they read each policy : the time they spent and how far they scrolled, so you can tell the difference between someone who read it properly and someone who opened it and marked it done. They can mark a policy as read at any point; we simply record what they actually did. Inside the reader there's also a “Talk to this Policy” button. It opens a focused chat where every answer comes straight from that one policy, and it suggests a few practical questions about it (in the staff member's language) to get them started, so if anything in the policy isn't clear, they can ask about it there and then.

title: Chat Hub
summary: Web-based chat interface for staff to ask policy questions, with role-tailored, rotating suggested questions in each staff member's language

blocks.title: What it does
blocks.text: The Chat Hub is a web page your staff can open on any device to ask questions about your policies. CareStream reads your uploaded documents and responds with a referenced answer, including the exact policy it drew from.

blocks.title: How staff access it
blocks.text: Staff visit your portal URL (shown in Settings under Portal access ). They enter their name and ask their question. No login is required unless you have enabled access restrictions.

blocks.title: Personalise the AI sign-off
blocks.text: Every answer CareStream gives your staff ends with a short sign-off line. To set your own, go to Settings → AI sign-off message , type the line you'd like (for example “The Crossways Care Team” or “Kind regards, the Management Team” ) and click Save . It applies to the next answer. Until you set your own, answers sign off as “The CareStream Team” .

blocks.title: Replying in the staff member's language
blocks.text: The “Reply in” picker under the message box now defaults to each staff member's own first language (the one set on their profile), so a Polish-speaking carer gets Polish answers straight away. They can still change it on the device, or leave it on a language of their choice; the picker lists all your available languages, including any you've added in Settings → Languages .

blocks.title: Voice — speak and listen
blocks.text: Staff don't have to type. The microphone button next to the message box lets them speak their question : and it now listens in their own language , not just English, so a carer can ask in Romanian or Tagalog by voice. Every answer also has a “Listen” button that reads the reply aloud in the answer's language, a real help for staff who find reading on a phone difficult, or who simply prefer to listen on shift.

blocks.title: What staff can ask
blocks.text: Staff choose a topic area before they start chatting. Each area uses a different knowledge source: Policies & Procedures: "What is the medication administration procedure?" Staff Handbook: "What are my annual leave entitlements?" Training & Learning: "Can you explain the key principles of safeguarding adults?" CQC Compliance: "What did the inspector say about our Well-led rating?" Auditing: "What actions are outstanding from our most recent audits?" Business Continuity: "What should I do if we have a serious staff shortage?"

blocks.title: Suggested questions are tailored to each staff member
blocks.text: When a staff member starts a new chat and picks a topic, the suggested starter questions aren't a fixed list, CareStream generates them for that person's job role . A nurse, a care assistant, a cook and a maintenance person will each see prompts relevant to their day-to-day work. The suggestions also rotate , so a returning staff member isn't shown the same three prompts every time, and they take account of what that person has recently asked , offering fresh, related questions rather than repeating ones they've already used. Everything is shown in the staff member's own language. To get the most from this: make sure each staff member has their Position set on their profile (Staff → add or edit a staff member). Staff with no position still get useful, rotating prompts, just not role-specific ones. There's nothing else to switch on, it works automatically.

blocks.title: Follow-up questions
blocks.text: After each response, CareStream shows three suggested follow-up questions. Staff can tap these to continue the conversation without typing.

blocks.title: Installing the hub as an app + notifications
blocks.text: Staff can install the hub to their phone's home screen so it opens like an app, no browser, no typing in a URL. When they open it on their phone they'll see a prompt: on Android it's an Install button; on iPhone they tap Share → Add to Home Screen . Once installed, the app offers to turn on notifications . With these on, staff get a tap on the shoulder when there's new training, a CQC practice question, or a renewal due, a proactive nudge landing straight in the hub. (Notifications are an extra: email still works as before.) Encourage your team to install the app and allow notifications, it's the easiest way to keep them engaged as more moves into the hub.

title: Email queries
summary: Staff can email policy questions and receive AI replies

blocks.title: How it works
blocks.text: CareStream provides a dedicated email address for your care setting (e.g. policies@yourcaresetting.carestreamai.co.uk ). When a staff member emails this address, CareStream reads the question, searches your policies, and replies directly to the thread.

blocks.title: Setting up your email address
blocks.text: Go to Settings and expand the Dedicated email address section. Your address is shown there. Share it with your team. Optionally add an allowlist to restrict which addresses can receive replies.

blocks.title: Thread continuity
blocks.text: CareStream remembers the conversation for 7 days. If a staff member replies to an AI response, it continues the same thread and they do not need to repeat context.

blocks.title: Intent routing
blocks.text: When the system is not sure whether an email is about a policy, training, or a CQC report, it sends a short clarification reply asking the staff member to choose. Once they reply with their choice, the conversation continues automatically.

title: CQC Report Chat
summary: Ask questions directly about your CQC inspection report

blocks.title: What it does
blocks.text: After uploading your CQC inspection report, staff can ask specific questions about it across all five key question domains (Safe, Effective, Caring, Responsive, Well-led). CareStream replies with the inspector's exact findings and the rating, citing the report.

blocks.title: Enabling CQC Report Chat
blocks.text: Go to Policies and upload your CQC report as a PDF. Select the category CQC Report . Wait for indexing to complete. The CQC Report Chat is now active on all channels.

blocks.title: Example questions
blocks.text: "What areas did the inspector flag as needing improvement?" "What was our Safe rating and what were the key findings?" "What did the report say about staffing levels?" "What actions do we need to take following the inspection?"

blocks.title: Built-in CQC knowledge
blocks.text: CareStream also includes a built-in library of CQC Key Questions covering all five domains. These are pre-loaded compliance frameworks that help answer general CQC questions even before your report is uploaded.

title: Annual training modules
summary: Standard or policy-tailored annual training, AI tokens, cover images, certificates & renewals

blocks.title: What it is
blocks.text: Annual training modules teach a topic then assess it. Each module has clear learning outcomes , an estimated duration , and an interactive lesson made of sections : every section teaches a point, then applies it with a real care scenario and a quick knowledge check : followed by the multiple-choice assessment. Staff complete them in the hub in their first language , and passing issues a certificate. Find it at Training → Annual training modules .

blocks.title: Two ways to get a module
blocks.text: Assign standard : a ready-made module from the CareStream standard library , written against good-practice care-sector guidance. These are free to assign and use none of your AI tokens. Quickest way to get started. Tailor to our policies : the AI reads your own uploaded policies (plus anonymised reference policies) and writes a module specific to how your home works, citing the policies it used. Tailoring a module uses AI tokens . Both kinds work identically for staff, the difference is only how the content was created. Start with standard modules and tailor the ones where your policies differ from the norm.

blocks.title: AI tokens
blocks.text: Tailoring modules, generating cover images and a few other AI features draw on your plan's monthly AI tokens (Starter 6 million, Professional 18 million, Enterprise 30 million). The remaining allowance is shown at the top of the Annual training page and on your dashboard. Tokens are separate from everyday questions staff ask in the hub, so running low on one never affects the other. The allowance resets on the 1st of each month. When it is spent you can still assign standard modules for free, or move up a plan. See AI tokens & your monthly allowance for the full picture.

blocks.title: Reviewing & approving
blocks.text: Open Annual training modules . You'll see a catalogue of UK care topics grouped by area, each with a default frequency and a practical-also-required flag where relevant. Use Assign standard (free) or Tailor to our policies (1 credit) on a topic. Tailored modules arrive as a draft with a lesson + question bank, citing the policies used. title: Training system
summary: Track staff training completion, send quiz questions, and answer training queries

blocks.title: Two kinds of training module
blocks.text: A module can be a full scenario-based lesson (a short lesson that teaches each point through a real care-home scenario, then a quick check, followed by an assessment) or a simpler assessment-only question set . Both are built on the Training → Adhoc Training Modules & Questions tab and taken by staff in the hub, in their first language.

blocks.title: Building a module — Adhoc Training Modules & Questions tab
blocks.text: Open Training → Adhoc Training Modules & Questions and use the buttons on each module: Generate lesson & questions (recommended) — the AI writes a full scenario lesson and a fresh assessment, grounded in your own policies, and reuses the matching standard module's images. The questions then open in the editor so you can review and Save . Questions only — generates just the assessment questions, with no lesson. Generate answer options — if you wrote your own question texts, this fills the A/B/C/D options. Preview — step through the lesson and questions read-only, exactly as staff will see it (appears once a module has a lesson). Save changes — saves your edits as a new version (kept in Question History). Lock / Unlock — date-stamps the exact questions in use, as CQC evidence of what was assessed and when.

blocks.title: What staff see (the hub)
blocks.text: Once you assign a module, it appears in the staff member's My Training in the hub. A module with a lesson plays step by step , the same way Annual training does: they read the lesson, work through the scenarios, then take the assessment, and a certificate is issued when they pass. An assessment-only module shows as a simple question list. Everything is in their first language.

blocks.title: Training in your team's language
blocks.text: Lessons and questions are automatically delivered in each staff member's first language. If their first language is set to Romanian, the lesson and answer options arrive in Romanian. No manual translation is needed. You set the language when adding a staff member on the Staff page; it can be changed at any time. It also applies to automated renewal reminders.

blocks.title: Scheduling question delivery
blocks.text: The Schedule Training Questions Delivery tab lets you set when training questions are sent out to staff (for example, a few questions a week), so training is drip-fed rather than landing all at once.

blocks.title: Asking questions about training topics
blocks.text: Staff are not limited to the assessment. They can ask open questions about any training topic at any time, through the Chat Hub, email, or voice. CareStream answers from your uploaded training materials and internal policies, bringing in relevant external regulatory guidance, and referencing the relevant CQC Key Questions where a topic overlaps an inspection area.

blocks.title: Viewing results
blocks.text: Go to Training → Compliance to see the live grid of every staff member against every assigned module (complete, in progress, expired), each person's score, and what's overdue. Individual records and the Analytics page give the same detail per person.
