title: Analytics & query history
summary: Understand what your staff are asking and how the AI is performing

blocks.title: Query history
blocks.text: Every query sent via any channel (web, email, voice) is logged. Go to Query history to see the full list, including the question, the AI response, which policies were cited, and whether the staff member gave feedback.

blocks.title: Analytics dashboard
blocks.text: Go to Analytics to see a summary of activity: total queries, most frequently asked topics, channel breakdown, and top staff users. This helps you identify gaps in your policies. If the same question is asked repeatedly, your policy on that topic may need to be clearer.

blocks.title: Engagement (weekly active staff)
blocks.text: Go to Analytics → Engagement for the single most important number as you move your team onto the staff hub: weekly active staff % . A staff member counts as active in a week if they opened the hub, asked a question, or read a policy. The tab also shows how many were active, your team size, and an 8-week trend so you can see the direction of travel. The channel mix shows where questions are coming in, hub vs email vs voice, over the last 30 days, with the hub's share called out. As you encourage staff onto the hub, you want weekly active % to hold steady (or rise) and the hub's share of questions to grow.

blocks.title: CQC report analytics
blocks.text: Go to Analytics and select CQC Report to see queries specifically about your inspection report. This shows which CQC domains your staff are most focused on.

blocks.title: Effectiveness of Training
blocks.text: Go to Analytics → Effectiveness of Training for evidence that your training and follow-up are genuinely improving knowledge, not just being completed. It draws entirely on data CareStream already collects, and it's the report to show CQC, commissioners and families when they ask what measurable difference your training makes. What it shows: Questions put right : how often a staff member got a question wrong, worked through the follow-up, then answered correctly. The core proof that gaps are being closed. Gaps resolved and engaged with learning : the share of knowledge gaps put right, and how often staff worked through the policy-grounded micro-lesson (“Learn & retry”) rather than just re-answering. Assessment accuracy and training completed : the team's current knowledge level and completion rate. Confidence to apply and rated useful : how staff rate the training after finishing it (see below). CQC prep improvement : the average score before and after a staff member reviews the model answer and retries. Language is not a barrier : completion and accuracy for staff who use second-language support compared with the rest of the team, an inclusion point for CQC. How staff rate their training: when a staff member finishes a piece of training, a short optional rating appears, how confident they feel applying it and how useful it was, with room for a comment. It shows across My Training , Annual Training , Follow-up and CQC Prep (on the completed item, or right after they finish it), and feeds the Confidence to apply and Rated useful figures. It only asks once per item and can always be skipped. These measures prove the training is landing, that staff react well to it, learn from it, and put it into practice. Linking training directly to care outcomes such as antipsychotic use, falls or incident rates is a planned next step that needs those outcomes to be recorded in CareStream.

blocks.title: Training Impact (does the training change practice?)
blocks.text: Analytics → Training Impact goes a step further: it shows whether your training is improving real, audited practice, not just quiz scores. You link an audit to the training module(s) it measures, and CareStream tracks that audit's compliance score over time alongside how many staff have completed the training. How to set it up: When you build your own audit (Monthly Audits, then Build your own audit ), tick the training module(s) it relates to under Linked training . For an audit you've already built, go to Monthly Audits and use the Linked training button on it to choose the modules. What you see: for each linked audit, the first and latest compliance score and the change between them, plus a month-by-month trend with two bars, the audit score and the cumulative training completion . If they rise together as staff complete the training, that is strong evidence the training is landing in practice. It needs several monthly audit runs to show a meaningful trend (one run is just a point), and it shows a correlation rather than proof of cause. Even so, it is exactly the continuous-improvement loop, train, audit, improve, re-audit, that CQC's “Well-led” question looks for. Linking currently works on your own custom audits.

title: Knowledge base
summary: Add and manage facts that CareStream always knows about your service, and resident profiles ("This is me")

blocks.title: What the knowledge base is for
blocks.text: The knowledge base lets you add short, structured facts about your care setting that CareStream always has access to. These are the things unique to your home that would not appear in a standard policy document, including what your staff need to know about individual residents, and they are exactly what makes chat answers specific to you. For example, you might have two COSHH storage cupboards : one under the stairs for substances in use, and one in the laundry room for unused stock. No policy would spell that out, but it is exactly what a staff member needs to know. Add it here and CareStream will use it when someone asks where COSHH substances are kept. The same applies to your registration number, registered manager, bed capacity, specialism, or emergency escalation contacts.

blocks.title: Where your knowledge comes from
blocks.text: The Knowledge Base page groups what CareStream knows into these types: Residents On the Professional and Enterprise plans: a profile for each current resident ("This is me"), shown first in its own colour. Click a resident to open the Residents screen on them. See "Resident profiles" below. Manual entries Facts you type in yourself, the home and care-setting nuances unique to your service (like the COSHH cupboards above). Shown first on the page because this is where your own knowledge lives. From uploaded policies Question-and-answer pairs CareStream generates automatically from the policy documents you upload. Use "Regenerate all" to (re)build them. CareStream standard entries A pre-loaded library of UK care regulatory knowledge (CQC Key Questions, health & safety, infection control, medication and more), provided as a starting point. You can edit these to make them specific to your home. They do not count against your document limit.

blocks.title: Approval, nothing goes live until you approve it
blocks.text: Every entry, whichever of the three types it is, is pending approval until you approve it, and only approved entries are ever used to answer staff or shown as a source in chat. This applies equally to your manual entries, the policy-generated ones, and the pre-loaded CareStream entries: pre-loaded entries are guides for what you could add, and you are meant to review, edit and approve them so they fit your home before staff ever see them. Go to Knowledge Base in the sidebar. For a manual fact, click Add entry , fill in the question and answer, and choose a Category (see below). For a pre-loaded or policy-generated entry, open it and edit it so it matches your home. Each entry shows a green Approved or amber Pending approval badge. Click Approve to make it live; you can Revoke at any time to take it back out of use. You will see a running count of approved vs pending entries at the top of the page. Staff only ever benefit from the approved ones.

blocks.title: Knowledge categories
blocks.text: The category you choose for a manual entry determines where it is used: General : available across all policy and handbook queries via the general knowledge base. Resident : no longer chosen here. Information about individual residents is now kept in Resident profiles, with the Residents button at the top of the page (see below). Business Continuity : appears exclusively in the Business Continuity chat channel. Staff can access it on the portal by selecting the Business Continuity card. Policies & Procedures, HR & Staff, Health & Safety, Medication, Infection Control : all feed into the general knowledge base and appear alongside relevant policy content.

blocks.title: Resident profiles: “This is me”
blocks.text: A policy tells your staff what the home does. A resident profile tells them about the person in front of them: what they like to be called, their life before they came to you, the food and music they love, what settles them at night, who matters to them. It is available on the Professional and Enterprise plans. Profiles are managed with the Residents button at the top of the Knowledge Base page, and each current resident also appears in a Residents group above your manual entries. Click a name to open the Residents screen on that person. A profile is about who they are, not their care record. Do not put medical, medication or safeguarding information in it. Keep that in the care plan. The Residents screen reminds you of this every time.

blocks.title: Adding a resident
blocks.text: Click Residents at the top of the Knowledge Base, then Add resident . Enter their first and last name, and if you like a preferred name, date of birth and room. Fill in as many of the eleven sections as you can: life story, interests, likes, dislikes, food and drink they enjoy, daily routine, what helps when they are upset or anxious, how they like to communicate, important people and pets, faith and traditions, and anything else. Each has a hint under it. Click Save . Staff can use the profile straight away. Because you wrote the profile, it does not need a separate approval. You can edit it whenever something changes, and the assistant uses the latest version.

blocks.title: Asking family and friends to add to it
blocks.text: The people who know a resident best are often their family and friends. You can invite them to tell you more, without giving them a login. Open the resident and go to the Family tab. Enter the person's name, email address and how they know the resident (for example daughter, son or friend), then click Send invitation . They receive an email with a private link to a short form. It asks one gentle question for each section, and they can answer as many or as few as they like. The link is just for them and stops working after 14 days. You can see whether each invitation has been sent, opened or answered. Use Resend to send a new link, or Revoke to cancel one. You can invite up to ten people for each resident. Each person gets their own link. If someone has already answered and wants to add more, resend their invitation. Want to show a colleague what a family member sees, without sending anything? Share the demonstration link carestreamai.com/family/demo . It uses a sample resident and home, never expires, and nothing typed into it is saved or sent.

blocks.title: Approving what they write, and checking it afterwards
blocks.text: Nothing a family member writes is shown to staff or used by the assistant until you approve it. That keeps you in control: a relative might mention a favourite treat that does not suit the person's diet, or something you would rather word differently. When someone answers, you get an email and a count appears on the resident's Approvals tab (and on their row in the Knowledge Base). Read each answer. Choose Approve , Edit then approve if you want to change the wording first, or Reject . Approved answers are added to the profile with the person's name and relationship after them, so staff can see who said it, for example “(Sally, daughter)”. To check what you have approved, open the From family tab. It lists each person who answered as a drawer: open one to see what they told you, when you approved it and who approved it. If you edited an answer first, you can still see what they originally wrote.

blocks.title: What staff see: asking about a resident
blocks.text: Once a home has at least one profile with content, staff see a This is me topic in the Chat Hub, in the sidebar and when they start a new chat. It works the same way as asking about a policy: they type a question about a resident and the chat answers, using only the profiles your home has written and approved. Ask about one person “What does Margaret like to drink?”, “What helps when Tom is anxious?” or “Tell me about Peggy before I go in.” Ask across everyone “Who enjoys music?” or “Who likes being outdoors?” finds the residents whose profiles mention it. If it is not recorded The chat says so plainly and suggests asking the person, their family or the team. It never makes something up, and it does not give medical advice: for anything clinical it points staff to the care plan. The answer names who a detail came from when family supplied it, and the profiles it used are listed under the answer. This is a fast way for a new starter, an agency worker or someone covering a shift to learn what the regular team already knows. Only current residents are included: when someone dies or moves on they are removed straight away.

blocks.title: When a resident dies or moves on
blocks.text: In the resident's Profile tab, use Mark as died or moved on in the red area at the bottom. Choose passed away or moved on, set the date and add a note if you want one. When you confirm: They disappear from the hub and from the assistant straight away. Any family invitations are cancelled and nothing waiting for approval can reach staff. The profile moves to Archived and is kept for seven years from the day it was archived. You can extend that date but not shorten it. The admins who can action archives get an email. Archived profiles are visible only to admins with archive access, from the Archived button in the Residents screen. Each one has four steps: Confirm the archive : say whether a memory book was shared with the family or they declined, add a note, and tick the box to remove the family's email addresses if you no longer need them. Download a copy as a text file, if you want one for a memory book or the record. Retention date , and extend it if the home needs to keep the profile longer. Delete the profile once the retention date has passed. You can delete earlier if you have a reason, which you must type in. You will be asked to type the resident's name to confirm. This cannot be undone. Who can action archives. Until you choose, every admin can. In the Archived view you can narrow it to named admins. Every view, download and deletion of an archived profile is logged.

blocks.title: Data protection
blocks.text: Resident profiles hold personal information about the people you support, and what family members tell you about them. Each home is responsible for using the feature in line with its own data protection approach: telling residents (or those acting for them) that a profile exists, covering it in your privacy notice, and deciding what is appropriate to record. Family answers are held for your approval and are never shown to staff automatically.

blocks.title: How your knowledge shows in chat answers, the source colours
blocks.text: When CareStream answers a staff question it lists what it drew from under “sources referenced” beneath the answer. Each kind of source has its own colour so staff (and inspectors) can see exactly where an answer came from: bg-teal Company policy One of your uploaded policy documents. Includes a "Read full policy" button to open the full text. bg-yellow-400 Home knowledge One of your approved manual knowledge base entries, the nuances unique to your home (e.g. the COSHH cupboards). bg-purple-500 CareStream guidance An approved pre-loaded CareStream regulatory entry that helped ground the answer. bg-blue-500 CareStream Seeded An external regulation the policy quotes (Care Act, COSHH, DoLS, and similar), labelled as CareStream seeded. Because of the approval gate above, a yellow “Home knowledge” or purple “CareStream guidance” source only ever appears once you have approved that entry.

The same applies to your registration number, registered manager, bed capacity, specialism, or emergency escalation contacts. Where your knowledge comes from The Knowledge Base page groups what CareStream knows into these types: Residents On the Professional and Enterprise plans: a profile for each current resident ("This is me"), shown first in its own colour. Click a resident to open the Residents screen on them. See "Resident profiles" below. Manual entries Facts you type in yourself, the home and care-setting nuances unique to your service (like the COSHH cupboards above). Shown first on the page because this is where your own knowledge lives. From uploaded policies Question-and-answer pairs CareStream generates automatically from the policy documents you upload. Use "Regenerate all" to (re)build them. CareStream standard entries A pre-loaded library of UK care regulatory knowledge (CQC Key Questions, health & safety, infection control, medication and more), provided as a starting point. You can edit these to make them specific to your home. They do not count against your document limit. Approval, nothing goes live until you approve it Every entry, whichever of the three types it is, is pending approval until you approve it, and only approved entries are ever used to answer staff or shown as a source in chat. This applies equally to your manual entries, the policy-generated ones, and the pre-loaded CareStream entries: pre-loaded entries are guides for what you could add, and you are meant to review, edit and approve them so they fit your home before staff ever see them. Go to Knowledge Base in the sidebar. For a manual fact, click Add entry , fill in the question and answer, and choose a Category (see below). Staff only ever benefit from the approved ones. Keep that in the care plan. The Residents screen reminds you of this every time. Adding a resident Click Residents at the top of the Knowledge Base, then Add resident . Enter their first and last name, and if you like a preferred name, date of birth and room. Fill in as many of the eleven sections as you can: life story, interests, likes, dislikes, food and drink they enjoy, daily routine, what helps when they are upset or anxious, how they like to communicate, important people and pets, faith and traditions, and anything else. Each has a hint under it. Click Save . Staff can use the profile straight away. Because you wrote the profile, it does not need a separate approval. You can edit it whenever something changes, and the assistant uses the latest version. Asking family and friends to add to it The people who know a resident best are often their family and friends. You can invite them to tell you more, without giving them a login. Open the resident and go to the Family tab. Enter the person's name, email address and how they know the resident (for example daughter, son or friend), then click Send invitation . They receive an email with a private link to a short form. It asks one gentle question for each section, and they can answer as many or as few as they like. The link is just for them and stops working after 14 days. Each person gets their own link. If someone has already answered and wants to add more, resend their invitation. Want to show a colleague what a family member sees, without sending anything? When someone answers, you get an email and a count appears on the resident's Approvals tab (and on their row in the Knowledge Base). Read each answer. Choose Approve , Edit then approve if you want to change the wording first, or Reject . Approved answers are added to the profile with the person's name and relationship after them, so staff can see who said it, for example “(Sally, daughter)”. Download a copy as a text file, if you want one for a memory book or the record. Retention date , and extend it if the home needs to keep the profile longer. Delete the profile once the retention date has passed. You can delete earlier if you have a reason, which you must type in. You will be asked to type the resident's name to confirm. This cannot be undone. Who can action archives. Until you choose, every admin can. In the Archived view you can narrow it to named admins. Every view, download and deletion of an archived profile is logged. Each home is responsible for using the feature in line with its own data protection approach: telling residents (or those acting for them) that a profile exists, covering it in your privacy notice, and deciding what is appropriate to record. Family answers are held for your approval and are never shown to staff automatically. How your knowledge shows in chat answers, the source colours When CareStream answers a staff question it lists what it drew from under “sources referenced” beneath the answer. Use the knowledge base for things that change less often than policies, such as your registration number, registered manager, bed capacity, or emergency escalation contacts. title: Business Continuity
summary: Give staff instant access to emergency procedures and contingency plans via the Chat Hub

blocks.title: What it does
blocks.text: The Business Continuity chat channel lets staff ask questions about your organisation's emergency procedures, escalation contacts, and contingency plans, directly from the staff portal. It reads exclusively from knowledge entries you have categorised as Business Continuity , so the answers are specific to your care setting.

blocks.title: Setting it up
blocks.text: Go to Knowledge Base in the sidebar and click Add entry . Write a question a staff member might ask (e.g. “What do I do if we have a power cut during a night shift?”) and the correct answer from your plan. Set the Category dropdown to Business Continuity . Optionally add the source name (e.g. “Business Continuity Plan v2”). Save and Approve the entry, only approved entries appear in responses. Repeat for all key scenarios: staff shortages, IT outages, fire/evacuation, adverse weather, utility failures, supplier failures, and key person absence.

blocks.title: How staff use it
blocks.text: Staff open the portal and click the Business Continuity card. They can then ask free-text questions such as: “We are two carers short tonight, what is the escalation process?” “Who do I call if the fire alarm system fails?” “What are the steps if we need to transfer residents to another facility?”

blocks.title: What to include
blocks.text: Suggested scenarios to cover in your Business Continuity entries: Staffing: serious shortage, key person absence, agency escalation contacts Utilities: power cut, water failure, heating failure procedures IT & communications: system outage, loss of internet, CCTV failure Building: fire, evacuation to assembly point, invacuation procedure Supplies: medication delivery failure, food supply disruption Regulatory: when to notify CQC, local authority, and next of kin

title: Face-to-face training
summary: Log in-person sessions, mark attendance and competency, track renewals in a compliance matrix, keep CQC evidence, and run a payroll report

blocks.title: What it's for
blocks.text: Most homes run in-person group training each month. The Face-to-face Training tab (under Training ) lets you record those sessions in a calendar , mark who attended and who missed, and keep evidence of both. It sits alongside the digital training, it does not change anyone's training matrix on its own; instead you decide who should also complete the module digitally.

blocks.title: Logging a session
blocks.text: Go to Training and open the Face-to-face Training tab, then click New session (or click a day in the calendar to open that day and add a session for it). Choose the training topic from the dropdown (the same modules you can assign digitally). The title fills in from the module; you can edit it. Set the date and the session length (1 to 5 hours), and record who delivered it , either a staff member or a free-typed name for an external trainer. The length sets how many hours off-shift attendees are owed on the payroll report. Optionally add a start/end time , location/room and capacity . To schedule a regular session, use Repeat to create a monthly series in one go (each copy carries the same details and allocated staff). Use Renews after if the training expires (e.g. 12 months) so the compliance matrix can track it. Tick the staff who were allocated to attend. For anyone who attended off shift , also tick Owed pay , this marks them as payable and owes them the session hours on the report. Leave it unticked for anyone who was on shift (already paid); by default nobody is owed. Then Create session . Add notes if useful.

blocks.title: Marking attendance
blocks.text: Open a session from the calendar and mark each person attended , missed , or leave them unmarked . Use All attended / All missed to set everyone at once, then adjust. This is your evidence of who was at each formal session.

blocks.title: Who gets paid: the “Owed pay” tick
blocks.text: Some staff attend training on shift (they're already being paid for that time) and some attend off shift on their own time (so they're owed the hours). The Owed pay tick is how you tell payroll who falls into the second group. Tick Owed pay next to anyone who attended off shift . They become payable and are owed hours equal to the session length (so a 2 hour session = 2 hours owed). Leave it unticked for anyone who was on shift. By default nobody is ticked, so you only tick the exceptions. The tick is all you need, you do not have to mark attendance first for it to count. The only thing that cancels pay is marking someone missed (absent), since they didn't attend. Example: a 2 hour Moving & Handling session with five staff. Three were on shift (leave unticked), two came in off shift (tick Owed pay ). The report shows those two as payable, 2 hours each, and a total of 4 hours owed. You can set this when you create the session or change it later: open the session, click Edit session , and adjust the ticks.

blocks.title: Reading the calendar
blocks.text: The calendar is colour-coded so you can see all training at a glance: teal for face-to-face sessions, orange for adhoc training and indigo for annual training, with +N allocated and ✓N completed counts. Click any day to open it and see the full detail: the face-to-face sessions that day (click through to mark attendance), plus the adhoc and annual training allocated or completed, by staff member.

blocks.title: Producing the monthly payroll report (PDF)
blocks.text: Click Payroll report at the top of the Face-to-face tab. Pick the month you're running payroll for. The summary shows how many face-to-face attendances are payable and the total hours owed. Click Download PDF to save it, or type an email address and click Send to email it as an attachment (for example to your payroll provider). The PDF carries the CareStream logo and the date it was generated , and separates training into three sections: Face-to-face (outlined in blue): one row per staff member per session, with the session length, attendance, a Pay? column and Hours owed . Payable rows (Owed pay ticked) are highlighted, and the section ends with a total hours owed for the month. Adhoc training : digital adhoc modules allocated and completed in the month. Annual training : annual modules allocated and completed in the month. Only face-to-face training carries a pay figure, adhoc and annual are for the training record, not payroll. If you set a training hourly rate on a staff member (edit their profile under Staff), the report also costs their owed hours into a £ total . Use CSV instead of the PDF to export the same data as a spreadsheet for your payroll system.

blocks.title: The compliance matrix
blocks.text: Switch the Face-to-face tab from Calendar to Matrix for an at-a-glance compliance grid: every staff member down the side, every training topic across the top. Each cell shows their latest attended session for that topic, colour-coded: In date — trained and still valid (or no expiry set). Due soon — valid but expires within 60 days. Overdue — past its renewal date (set Renews after on the session to drive this). Missing — the topic is mandatory for their role and they don't hold it. Use Mandatory by role to choose which training each job role must hold. Anyone in that role without it is flagged missing , so you can see your gaps before an inspection. The chips at the top total your overdue, due-soon and missing counts.

blocks.title: Evidence for CQC (sign-in sheets, files, certificates)
blocks.text: Open a session and use the Evidence panel to build a defensible record: Sign-in sheet : download a printable register (session details + a signature line per allocated staff member). Staff sign on the day, then you scan it. Upload file : attach the signed scan, photos, or the trainer's certificate (PDF or image, up to 15 MB). Files are stored privately and open with a click. Competency : for each attendee, record competent or not yet competent where the training was practically assessed. The Evidence panel always shows an “Uploaded files” list with a count, so you can see exactly what is held against a session, and it tells you clearly when nothing has been uploaded yet. On the calendar, any session that has evidence shows a small paperclip with the file count, so you can spot at a glance which sessions have their paperwork. Uploaded files are kept safe automatically: every file is checked to confirm it is a genuine PDF or image and scanned for malware before it is stored. Anything that fails is rejected and never saved, and a small scanned tag shows on files that passed.

blocks.title: Evidence log (everything in one place)
blocks.text: Click Evidence log at the top of the Face-to-face tab (next to Payroll report ) to see every file uploaded across all sessions in one list, grouped by training session with its date and file count. Open any file with a click, or click a session to jump straight to it. It is the quickest way to answer an inspector who asks to see your face-to-face training records, without opening each session one by one.

blocks.title: Completion certificates (issued and tracked)
blocks.text: In a session, each attendee has a Certificate button. It produces a branded, full-page completion certificate named after the course and date. Attended only : the button activates once you mark the person attended (the green tick). You can't issue a certificate to someone who missed or isn't marked yet. Saved automatically : issuing a certificate downloads it and stores it against that staff member. A tick on the button shows one has been issued; re-issuing replaces it. On the staff record : every certificate appears in a Training certificates section on the individual's staff page (Staff → open a person), where you can re-open any of them. In analytics : Analytics → Staff shows a Completion certificates list across all staff, plus a per-person count, so you have one place to see and open everything issued.

blocks.title: Reminding allocated staff by email
blocks.text: Reminders are never sent automatically , you decide when. While creating a session, use Create & email reminder to create it and email the allocated staff that they're booked in. For an existing session, open it and click Email reminder to allocated staff (handy to send again closer to the date). The session shows when a reminder was last sent .

blocks.title: Sending the digital module to anyone who missed
blocks.text: In the session, the Send the digital module panel lets you pick exactly who should complete the training digitally, click Select those who missed for the obvious case, or choose anyone. They get the module in their hub My Training , and the session shows a sent marker against them. A module can only be sent once it has been built (it has a lesson or questions). If it hasn't, you'll see a prompt to add a lesson or questions in Training → Adhoc Training Modules & Questions first, and unbuilt topics are marked “not built yet” in the session form.

blocks.title: Backfilling the last 12 months
blocks.text: To get started, add your past sessions : create a session as normal but set a past date , pick the topic and trainer, and mark who attended/missed. This builds up your history so the record and analytics reflect the training you've already delivered.

blocks.title: Planning ahead
blocks.text: Use the calendar arrows to move into next year and schedule future sessions. From October each year, a reminder appears prompting you to start planning the following year if nothing is booked yet.

blocks.title: Seeing it across the platform
blocks.text: You can review face-to-face training in three places: Analytics → Staff : a Face-to-face training section showing who missed sessions, who was sent the digital module as a result, and whether they've completed it. The hub : an admin-only F2F Training tab gives you the same picture on your phone. Each staff record : a Face-to-face training section listing the sessions that person was allocated to, whether they attended or missed, and the status of any catch-up module. It's part of their record for CQC evidence.

title: Training Matrix
summary: Set the training each job role needs, then see every staff member against it in one grid with face-to-face and safe to work checks, and export it for inspection

blocks.title: What it's for
blocks.text: The Training Matrix tab (under Training , next to Face-to-face Training) answers the question an inspector asks first: is every member of staff trained for the job they do? It shows each staff member against the training their job role requires , so a cook and a nurse are each measured against their own list, and gaps are flagged even when the training was never assigned.

blocks.title: Set the training each role needs
blocks.text: Go to Training and open the Training Matrix tab. Click Required training by role . Pick All staff for training everyone needs, then tick the courses. Pick each job role in turn and tick the extra courses that role needs, then click Save requirements . title: CQC Staff Prep
summary: Build staff confidence for CQC inspector interviews with practice questions and AI-scored answers

blocks.title: What it is
blocks.text: CQC Staff Prep helps your team prepare for conversations with CQC inspectors. Staff are sent open-ended practice questions, the kind an inspector would actually ask, and write their answers in their own words. CareStream evaluates each answer and gives a score out of 100 with specific feedback, so staff know exactly where to improve before an inspection.

blocks.title: How it works
blocks.text: Go to CQC Staff Prep in the Reporting section of the sidebar. The Question Bank comes pre-loaded with 21 CQC inspector-style questions organised across five domains: Safe, Effective, Caring, Responsive, and Well-led. Each question shows its model answer : the standard a strong answer is measured against, and its own tracking line: how many staff it's been assigned to, how many have answered , and their average score . To send a question out, use Assign to all staff to send it to everyone at once, or Assign to specific staff to pick individuals. A domain header also has Assign all to staff to send every question in that domain in one go. (Admins are never included, only active staff are assigned.) The question is automatically rephrased before delivery so staff cannot memorise the exact wording. (If someone already has that question, they aren't sent a duplicate.) Staff open their portal and write a free-text answer. There is no multiple choice, they must articulate their knowledge in their own words, just as they would with a real inspector. CareStream immediately scores the answer from 0 to 100, against the model answer, and gives constructive written feedback. Staff see their result, and the model answer , straight away. If a staff member scores below 60, they can review the model answer and feedback, then try again in their own words. The new attempt is re-scored and replaces the old one, so the follow-up is built in, no manual re-sending needed. Track progress across your whole team in the Performance tab, scores are shown per staff member and per CQC domain so you can see exactly where to focus.

blocks.title: Send role-matched questions (recommended)
blocks.text: The quickest way to prepare the whole team is the Send role-matched questions panel at the top of the page. Pick who should practise and CareStream generates and sends everything in one step. Three dropdowns control what each person receives (each has an (i) hover on the page as a reminder): Role-specific questions each : questions tailored to each person's job, the chef gets food safety and allergens, nurses get medicines and clinical care. Everyone in the same role receives the same set, so colleagues can practise together. Core questions for everyone : topics every member of staff must be able to answer in an inspection, safeguarding, whistleblowing and fire safety, sent to all selected staff regardless of role. Standard CQC question set : the four themes inspectors raise with staff in almost every inspection, reworded freshly each time so staff practise the substance, not a script. What you enjoy about your role Inspectors want to hear what you love about working at the service and how your work has made a positive difference to people’s lives. If there is something you are particularly proud of, share the story: inspectors value real examples of meaningful impact. Your experience of raising concerns If you have ever raised a concern about the quality of care, inspectors want to understand what happened next. Were you listened to? What actions were taken? The need for improvement does not automatically mean a service is poor; inspectors look at how issues are raised and how the provider responds. How you support people day-to-day Inspectors want to know about the people you care for, how you understand and meet their needs, and how the service shares information within the team to achieve the best outcomes for those you support. The support you get in your role Inspectors want to know that you are supported by your line managers, that you know where to go when you need help, and that you have had the training and support you need in your role. . You can also scope the send to particular CQC domains with the domain chips. The estimated AI tokens cost is shown before you press Generate & send.

blocks.title: The five CQC domains
blocks.text: Safe Safeguarding, medication, infection control, risk management, and responding to incidents. Effective Person-centred care, nutrition and hydration, independence, consent, and staff training. Caring Dignity and respect, communication, emotional wellbeing, and family involvement. Responsive Meeting individual needs, handling complaints, and responding to changes in condition. Well-led Open reporting culture, team communication, following policies, and raising concerns.

blocks.title: Adding your own questions
blocks.text: Click Add question in the Question Bank to create a single CQC prep question. You can write it manually, or describe a topic and let CareStream draft the question and model answer for you using AI. To create several at once, click Generate with AI . Choose a single domain or a balanced mix across all five , pick how many (3, 5 or 10), and optionally give a focus theme (e.g. dementia care, medication). CareStream generates that many brand-new questions and model answers, saves them straight to your bank, and avoids duplicating questions you already have. All generated questions follow the same CQC inspector style and include a model answer used for scoring. Generating questions draws on your AI tokens , in proportion to how much is generated: a batch of five uses roughly five times one. Your remaining allowance is shown before you confirm.

blocks.title: Understanding scores
blocks.text: 80–100 Excellent Covers all key points clearly, staff would reassure an inspector on this topic. 60–79 Good Solid knowledge with minor gaps. A little more detail would strengthen the answer. 40–59 Partial Some good points but significant gaps. An inspector would probe further. 0–39 Needs work Key knowledge is missing or vague. This area needs focused attention before an inspection.

blocks.title: Learn & retry
blocks.text: After answering, staff see the model answer. If they score below 60 they get a Review & try again option: they read the model answer and feedback, then re-answer in their own words. The new attempt is re-scored and replaces the old one, and we keep their first score so the improvement is recorded, built-in follow-up, with no manual re-sending.

blocks.title: Tracking & evidence
blocks.text: In the Question Bank , each question shows how many staff it's been assigned to, how many answered, and the average score. In Analytics → CQC Staff Prep , you get the whole-team picture: scores by inspection domain, a per-staff table, and a Review & retry summary showing how many answers were re-attempted and the average score improvement, direct evidence staff are learning. On each staff record , a CQC Staff Prep section lists every question that person was assigned, their score, and any improvement after retrying. It's included in the CQC evidence PDF.

title: Policy gaps
summary: Identify missing or incomplete policies in your document library

blocks.title: What it does
blocks.text: Policy Gaps checks the regulations that apply to a registered care setting against the actual content of your uploaded policies, it reads inside the documents rather than matching on titles. For each regulation it tells you whether your policies cover it, partially cover it, or leave a gap , and names the policy that provides the evidence. It also surfaces unanswered staff questions : recurring themes where staff asked something the assistant couldn't answer from your policies, which is real-world evidence of a missing or unclear policy.

blocks.title: How coverage is judged
blocks.text: CareStream keeps a library of the regulations that apply to registered care settings (CQC fundamental standards, the Care Act, health & safety law, MCA/DoLS, infection control, and more). For each one, the coverage check works in three steps: Find the relevant policy passages. The regulation is turned into a search and run against the indexed content of all your uploaded policies, the same retrieval that powers the staff chat, to pull out the passages most likely to address it. Judge from the content. An AI compliance auditor reads those passages and decides, from your documents' actual wording, not their titles, whether they substantively address the regulation. Record the verdict and evidence. Each regulation is marked Covered, Partial or Gap, with the policy that provides the evidence and a one-line reason. Results are cached so the page is instant until you re-run it. This is the key difference from a simple checklist: a regulation is only flagged when your policies genuinely don't address it in content, so with a complete, well-maintained library the vast majority come back Covered.

blocks.title: Covered, Partial and Gap
blocks.text: Covered A policy clearly and substantively addresses the regulation. The evidence policy is named. Partial The topic is touched on but the policy is incomplete for what the regulation requires. The policy that partly covers it is named so you can strengthen it. Gap Nothing in your uploaded policies addresses the regulation, add a policy that covers it.

blocks.title: Unanswered staff questions
blocks.text: Alongside regulation coverage, the page clusters questions your staff asked, in the Chat Hub, by email or by voice, that the assistant could not answer from your policies in the last 90 days. Recurring themes here are real-world evidence that a policy is missing, unclear, or not yet uploaded, straight from how your team actually uses CareStream.

blocks.title: Using policy gaps
blocks.text: Go to Policy Gaps in the sidebar. Click Run coverage analysis . CareStream reads through your policies and judges each regulation against their content, this takes about a minute. The result is saved, so re-open the page any time; re-run it after you've uploaded or updated policies. Review anything flagged as a Gap or Partial . Each shows why, and partials name the policy that partly covers it. For each gap, upload a policy that addresses it (or strengthen the partial one). Re-run the analysis to confirm it's now covered.

title: Monthly Audits
summary: Run, schedule, sign off and track care quality audits, build or import your own, and follow every action through to the re-check

blocks.title: What audits do
blocks.text: The Audits module gives you a library of 100+ ready-made audits covering the governance of a care setting, plus the tools to build or import your own. Audits can be completed on the web or on a phone or tablet in the Chat Hub , scheduled and assigned to named staff, signed and approved, and turned into an action plan that is followed through to a re-check at the next audit. Every completed audit produces a PDF report and feeds the Trends panel, so you can show inspectors not just that you audit, but that things improve.

blocks.title: The audit library
blocks.text: Every built-in audit is written for UK care settings and each question is tagged with the CQC quality statement it evidences. Daily Fire Marshall Checklist, Daily Medication Audit, Resident Bedrooms (room by room), Fluid Intake and Hydration (per resident) Weekly Medication Stock and Storage Monthly Health and Safety, Medicines Management, Kitchen, Accident and Incident Book, Resident Bedroom Audit, Care Plan Review, Resident Feedback Round, Staff Training and Compliance, Monthly Governance Review, Safeguarding Log Review, Night Shift Walkround, Premises and Maintenance, Mealtime Experience, Falls Prevention and Post-Fall Review, Pressure Care and Skin Integrity, Water Safety and Legionella, Laundry, Call Bell Response Quarterly Infection Control, Fire Drill Record, Single Assessment Framework Review, Dementia Care Environment, HR Staff Files (per staff member) Periodic Quality Assurance, GDPR Audit Checklist Click Preview on any audit to read every question exactly as it will be asked, before you use it. In the preview, click Edit questions to make small changes: reword a question, change its answer type, or add a question to a section. Your edited version replaces the standard one in your list, and Restore original in the preview brings the standard audit back (your completed audits are kept). On the Free, Starter and Professional plans you can add up to 2 extra questions to an audit; Enterprise has no limit and can also build audits from scratch. Wording and answer-type changes are not counted.

blocks.title: Building your own audit
blocks.text: On the Monthly Audits page click Build your own audit . Give it a name , choose how often it runs, and whether it is done once for the home , room by room , per resident or per staff member . Tick shift if the auditor should record which shift it covers. Add sections , then add questions to each one and choose a type for each question (see the table below). Optionally make a question conditional , so it is only asked when an earlier answer matches (for example “What was the discrepancy?” only when the balance check finds one). Optionally tag each question with the CQC quality statement it evidences. The tags appear in the report and help the AI recommendations. Under Linked training , tick any training module this audit measures, so Analytics → Training Impact can show whether the training improved the scores. Click Create audit . It appears under Available audits alongside the built-in ones. Yes / No / N/A A check that is met, not met, or does not apply. A “No” asks what was found and what will be done. Yes / No The same, where not applicable is not an option. Number A reading or count with an optional unit and pass range, for example a fridge between 2 and 8 °C. Readings outside the range fail. Date A date to record, such as the last service. Choice Pick one option. Mark any option that shows a problem as a fail. Multiple choice Tick all that apply, with the same fail marking. Rating A score out of a maximum you choose, with an optional pass mark. Findings Written findings with actions and timescales. Free text A note that is not scored, such as who was spoken to. Custom audits work everywhere the built-in ones do: scheduling, the hub, signatures, PDF reports, action plans and trends. Building, copying and importing audits are included on the Enterprise plan.

blocks.title: Importing an audit you already use
blocks.text: Already have audits on paper or in Word? You do not need to retype them. Click Import an existing audit on the Monthly Audits page. Upload a PDF , a Word document , a text file, or a photo of the paper form (up to 15 MB). Scanned and handwritten forms work. AI reads it and opens it in the builder with the sections, question types, options, conditions and CQC tags filled in. Anything it was unsure about is listed at the top under Worth checking . Check and edit it, then click Create audit . Nothing is saved until you do. Each import uses one AI credit.

blocks.title: Editing audits and versions
blocks.text: Click Edit on any of your audits to change it. Every save creates a new version , and you can add a short note saying what changed. Click Versions to see the full history of who changed what and when. Completed audits always keep the exact questions they were answered against, so changing a question never rewrites an old report. That gives you a clear record for inspectors of how your audits have developed.

blocks.title: Scheduling and assigning audits
blocks.text: In Scheduled audits on the Monthly Audits page, click Schedule an audit . Choose the audit, the room, resident or staff member if it has one, the person it is assigned to , the due date and whether it repeats . Staff who are not admins are given access to that audit automatically. The person sees it in the hub under Assigned to you . When they complete it, the schedule is marked done and the next one is set up from the repeat. Use the filters on the Schedule tab ( Overdue , Due in 7 days , All open , Done and missed ) to see where things stand. A repeat that passes without being done is recorded as missed. The assigned person is emailed when an audit is assigned, two days before it is due, and when it becomes overdue. In Settings → Audits you choose when an overdue audit is escalated to admins and managers, and whether admins get a summary email weekly, daily or not at all. Each staff member's record also lists the audits scheduled for them.

blocks.title: Calendar and matrix: keeping on top of what is due
blocks.text: Above your scheduled audits there are three tabs: Schedule (the list described above), Calendar and Matrix . They are on every plan and show the whole home, so an admin can see at a glance what is due on which day and what has and has not been done. Which audits appear Only the audits you have scheduled or added by hand . Nothing is listed until you choose it, so you are never shown audits as “missed” that you never meant to do. Scheduling an audit adds it automatically. To track an audit you are not scheduling, open the Matrix , pick it from Add an audit to the matrix and click Add . Audits you added by hand have a small × to take them off again. The Calendar A month view, Monday first. Each audit appears on the day it is due, coloured by state: teal due, amber in progress, green done, red overdue or missed. Audits completed without being scheduled appear on the day they were completed. Click a day to see everything on it, who it is assigned to, and open a started or completed audit. Use the arrows or Today to move between months. The line under the month shows how many are overdue, still to do and done. The Matrix One row for each audit on your board and one column for each of the last six months. Use the arrows to move back in steps of three months. Each cell shows Done , In progress , Due , Overdue , Missed or Not done . Daily audits show how many were done that month. Not done (red) appears only for audits that should happen at least monthly (daily, weekly or monthly), and only from the month you scheduled or added the audit. Quarterly and periodic audits are never marked red just for being quiet in a month. Completed audits count towards a month whether or not they were scheduled. They are matched by audit and month, so audits you have already done show up straight away for the audits on your board. Want a regular rhythm? Schedule each audit with a repeat. The calendar then fills ahead, the matrix turns green as they are completed, and reminders and escalation work as described above.

blocks.title: Completing an audit on the web
blocks.text: Go to Monthly Audits and click New audit . Choose the audit and the month, plus the room, resident, staff member or shift if it asks for one. Click Start audit . If this audit has been done before, Actions from the last audit appear first. Check each one and mark it Still fixed or Not fixed . Not fixed reopens the action for the person it was assigned to. Work through each section. Conditional questions appear only when they apply. Answers save automatically, and Save & exit lets you come back later from In progress . Open the Summary tab and add strengths, areas for improvement and a target date for actions. Every question that is showing must be answered before you can finish. Sign with your finger or mouse and type your name. Then click Complete & get AI recommendations , or Send to care manager for approval if manager approval is switched on.

blocks.title: Doing audits in the Chat Hub
blocks.text: Admins, and staff given audit access or assigned an audit, get an Audits item in the hub, ideal for walking the home with a phone or tablet. Open Audits in the hub. Anything Assigned to you is at the top with its due date, then anything in progress, then every audit grouped by how often it runs. Answer each question. Where something is wrong, take a photo and draw on it to circle or arrow the problem before it is saved to the audit. Sign on screen and complete. Hub audits are the same records as the web, so they appear in the repository, reports and trends straight away.

blocks.title: Per-room, per-resident and per-staff audits
blocks.text: Some audits are done one at a time : bedrooms room by room, care plans and hydration per resident, HR files per staff member. You choose who or which room when you start, and each is tracked as its own record. Set how many rooms your home has in Settings → Rooms . The room picker then offers 1 to that number. Need a named room (for example “Lavender”)? Type it into the room box when starting and it is remembered for next time.

blocks.title: Manager sign-off

title: Managing multiple homes (Group)
summary: Benchmark every home in your group and switch between them

blocks.title: What the Group console is
blocks.text: If your organisation runs more than one home, they can be linked together as a group . A Group item then appears at the top of the sidebar (you only see it when your account has more than one site). It gives regional and head-office managers a single place to see how every home is doing and to jump straight into any one of them.

blocks.title: The group overview
blocks.text: Open Group to see: Summary cards across the whole group: number of homes, total staff, and group-wide Training, Onboarding, Audits and an Overall compliance score. title: Workforce compliance register (Enterprise)
summary: DBS, right to work, registration, references, document uploads, expiry alerts, supervisions and appraisals

blocks.title: What it is
blocks.text: The Workforce compliance register is an Enterprise feature . It keeps each staff member's “safe to work” credentials in one place, with expiry dates and a live Red/Amber/Green view. It is the evidence CQC looks for under safe recruitment (Regulation 19), so nothing quietly lapses. Open it from Compliance in the Team section of the sidebar. It tracks five credentials per person: DBS check (certificate number and renewal date) Right to work (document type, plus expiry for time-limited visas) Passport (number and expiry date, important for overseas staff) Professional registration (for example NMC, with renewal date) References (received or outstanding)

blocks.title: The register
blocks.text: The register shows every active staff member with a colour-coded status for each credential: green when it is valid, amber when it expires within 30 days, and red when it is expired or missing. The summary cards at the top total how many are valid, expiring soon, expired or missing across your whole team.

blocks.title: Recording a credential
blocks.text: Click a staff member's row to open their compliance record. For each credential, enter the reference (for example the DBS certificate number), the issue date, and the expiry or renewal date, then click Save . The register updates straight away, and the colour reflects the new expiry date. Use Clear to remove a credential if it was added by mistake.

blocks.title: Uploading the documents
blocks.text: You can attach the actual document to each credential (the DBS certificate, visa, registration card or reference letter). Open a staff member's record from the register and use Upload next to a credential to add a PDF or image (up to 15 MB). Files are validated and virus-scanned before they are stored securely. Once uploaded, a paperclip appears on that credential in the register, and you can View or Replace the document at any time. Each staff member's record page also has a Compliance credentials section showing their status and letting you open the uploaded documents, so everything is together as CQC evidence.

blocks.title: Expiry alerts
blocks.text: CareStream can email your admins a digest of any credentials that have expired or expire within the next 30 days, so renewals never slip. This runs automatically each day. You can turn it on or off under Settings → Email communications → Compliance credential expiry . You can also send it on demand: on the Compliance page, click Email expiry alerts at the top right and your admins get the digest straight away. Passports are treated a little differently: as well as the admin digest, the staff member is emailed personally as their passport comes up for renewal (and if it has expired), so overseas staff can keep it valid. All of these emails use the Compliance credential expiry toggle under Settings.

blocks.title: Supervisions and appraisals
blocks.text: The Supervisions & appraisals tab on the Compliance page is where you book and track each staff member's 1:1 supervisions and annual appraisals, showing their last session and next booked or due date, colour coded so overdue ones stand out. Supervisions and appraisals are part of the Enterprise plan , and they have their own recording form, agreed-action tracking and allocation flow. On Enterprise, they also link to training: see Training and supervisions, linked . See the dedicated Supervisions guide below for the full flow: booking, choosing who conducts it, completing the recording form, and allocating training, induction or CQC prep off the agreed actions.

title: Supervisions
summary: Book supervisions and appraisals, record them on a structured form, and allocate the training, induction or CQC prep that comes out of them

blocks.title: What it is, available on the Enterprise plan
blocks.text: Supervisions let you book and record each staff member's 1:1 supervisions and annual appraisals, complete a structured recording form, and turn what you agree into actions and allocations that land straight in the staff member's hub. It is part of the Enterprise plan , in the Compliance area. Every completed session is kept on the staff member's record as CQC evidence. You book and track sessions from Compliance → Supervisions & appraisals in the Team section of the sidebar. The whole flow has three stages: book the session and choose who conducts it, the conductor records it on the form, and the agreed actions are allocated to the staff member.

blocks.title: 1. Booking a session and choosing who conducts it
blocks.text: Open the Compliance page and switch to the Supervisions & appraisals tab. Click a staff member and use Log a session . Choose supervision or appraisal , the date, an optional next-due date, and any notes. Set Conducted by . This is a dropdown of your administrators, so you can allocate the person who will carry out the session rather than typing a name. Choose a future date to book an upcoming session, or a past date to record one already held. Booked sessions show as Booked on the register with their date. The person you pick under “Conducted by” is notified straight away: they get a message in their own hub , and an email, telling them they are conducting this staff member's session on the date. The staff member and your admins are notified too.

blocks.title: 2. Recording the supervision on the form
blocks.text: The conductor completes the session on a structured recording form, in the style of the Skills for Care supervision template. They open it from their own hub, under Supervisions I'm conducting , next to the booked session. The form is pre-filled with the staff member being supervised , the supervisor (from your admin list), and the date . It captures ten sections: Actions from the previous meeting Biggest achievement since the last supervision Continuing to display the values of the organisation Challenges faced, and how they were overcome Any challenges that remain, and what is needed Learning and development done, and how it has been put into practice What to achieve before the next supervision Feedback from the supervisor Other areas of discussion Agreed actions The conductor also sets the next supervision date on the form. When they Save & complete , the session is recorded and saved against the staff member.

blocks.title: 3. Agreed actions become the staff member's to-do list
blocks.text: Each agreed action is a free-text line. On completion, every action is written into the staff member's hub under My actions , so it works as a shared to-do list. The staff member can mark each one Start , Done or reopen it, and the same actions show on their record page so you can see they are being handled.

blocks.title: 4. Allocating training, induction or CQC prep from an action
blocks.text: Next to each agreed action, the conductor can choose to allocate something to the staff member. Pick a type, then a second dropdown lists that item from your account: Training Allocate a training module from your ad-hoc training list. It appears in the staff member’s My training. Induction Allocate one of your staff onboarding flows. It appears in the staff member’s Induction. CQC prep Allocate a CQC prep question. It appears in the staff member’s CQC section. When you complete the form, the chosen item is sent to the staff member exactly as if you had allocated it the usual way, with the same email and hub notification, and it shows on their analytics page. It is safe to re-save a completed form: an item that has already been allocated is not sent twice.

blocks.title: Saved against the staff member
blocks.text: Every completed supervision is saved on the staff member's record page , listed under their supervisions with a link to open the full form and the next session booked off it. Any items allocated from an action show a small badge on the record, so you can see at a glance what came out of each session. The register keeps colour-coding the last and next dates so overdue supervisions stand out. Staff can see their own booked and past sessions in their hub under Supervisions . You can turn the confirmation and reminder emails on or off under Settings → Email communications → Supervisions & appraisals .

blocks.title: Training and supervisions, linked
blocks.text: Supervisions are where a manager decides what someone needs, and training is how it gets done. CareStream links the two, so you go into a supervision knowing how the person is doing on their training, and what you agree turns into training that closes itself. The training brief. Before the meeting, open the person from Compliance → Supervisions & appraisals , or open the recording form in your hub, and expand Training brief . It shows what is overdue, due soon or expired, low scores, what they have finished since the last supervision, CQC prep gaps, unanswered questions and open actions, with a short Worth raising list. The training in full. Press See the training in full for a card per course: status, dates, score, time on the lesson, the pre-course check, and every question answered wrongly with their answer and the correct one. With more than one course, each is an accordion that starts closed with a one-line summary, and Open all opens them together. Suggestions, inside each course. Open a course and, at the bottom, you will find ideas for the conversation about that course: for example a low score on a topic, a clear learning gain, a course that is overdue, or all attempts used. Anything that spans more than one course, such as low scores on several, sits in a box at the top. Each suggestion shows the evidence it is based on. They are worked out from the scores and answers by fixed rules, not by AI, so they cost nothing and are the same every time. They are prompts, not judgements, and short courses are worded as “worth checking”. Add as agreed action puts one on the supervision. Allocated training still to do. A closed box near the top lists everything allocated to them that is not finished, of every kind: CPD courses, annual training, ad hoc training and face to face sessions. It is grouped as Missed (past the due date, or a face to face session they did not attend), Part done , Not started , and Not recorded (a face to face session that has passed with no attendance marked, so nobody has said they missed it). A course that has been renewed since, or a missed session made up with the digital catch-up, is not listed. Print or email it. Use Print for a clean page with the CareStream logo, or Send to email to send it to yourself or another administrator on the account. It can only go to an administrator, because it holds a staff member's training records. Allocate training to a supervision. When you assign a course, tick Also add to their next supervision . It adds an action to each person's next booked supervision, and the action closes by itself when they complete the course. Nothing is added unless you tick it, and nothing is created for someone with no supervision booked. A snapshot in the record. When a supervision is completed, a short summary of their training at that time is saved in the record, so it shows what was true on the day. It cannot be edited afterwards. The brief, the training detail and the suggestions are for the supervisor and administrators only. Staff do not see them, but they can see the actions that come out of the supervision in their hub. Tell your staff in your policies that their training results may be discussed in supervisions.

It is part of the Enterprise plan , in the Compliance area. Every completed session is kept on the staff member's record as CQC evidence. You book and track sessions from Compliance → Supervisions & appraisals in the Team section of the sidebar. The whole flow has three stages: book the session and choose who conducts it, the conductor records it on the form, and the agreed actions are allocated to the staff member. 1. Booking a session and choosing who conducts it Open the Compliance page and switch to the Supervisions & appraisals tab. Click a staff member and use Log a session . Choose supervision or appraisal , the date, an optional next-due date, and any notes. Set Conducted by . This is a dropdown of your administrators, so you can allocate the person who will carry out the session rather than typing a name. Choose a future date to book an upcoming session, or a past date to record one already held. Booked sessions show as Booked on the register with their date. The person you pick under “Conducted by” is notified straight away: they get a message in their own hub , and an email, telling them they are conducting this staff member's session on the date. The staff member and your admins are notified too. 2. Recording the supervision on the form The conductor completes the session on a structured recording form, in the style of the Skills for Care supervision template. They open it from their own hub, under Supervisions I'm conducting , next to the booked session. The form is pre-filled with the staff member being supervised , the supervisor (from your admin list), and the date . It captures ten sections: Actions from the previous meeting Biggest achievement since the last supervision Continuing to display the values of the organisation Challenges faced, and how they were overcome Any challenges that remain, and what is needed Learning and development done, and how it has been put into practice What to achieve before the next supervision Feedback from the supervisor Other areas of discussion Agreed actions The conductor also sets the next supervision date on the form. When they Save & complete , the session is recorded and saved against the staff member. 3. Agreed actions become the staff member's to-do list Each agreed action is a free-text line. On completion, every action is written into the staff member's hub under My actions , so it works as a shared to-do list. The staff member can mark each one Start , Done or reopen it, and the same actions show on their record page so you can see they are being handled. 4. Allocating training, induction or CQC prep from an action Next to each agreed action, the conductor can choose to allocate something to the staff member. Pick a type, then a second dropdown lists that item from your account: Training Allocate a training module from your ad-hoc training list. It appears in the staff member’s My training. Induction Allocate one of your staff onboarding flows. It appears in the staff member’s Induction. CQC prep Allocate a CQC prep question. It appears in the staff member’s CQC section. When you complete the form, the chosen item is sent to the staff member exactly as if you had allocated it the usual way, with the same email and hub notification, and it shows on their analytics page. It is safe to re-save a completed form: an item that has already been allocated is not sent twice. Saved against the staff member Every completed supervision is saved on the staff member's record page , listed under their supervisions with a link to open the full form and the next session booked off it. Any items allocated from an action show a small badge on the record, so you can see at a glance what came out of each session. The register keeps colour-coding the last and next dates so overdue supervisions stand out. Staff can see their own booked and past sessions in their hub under Supervisions . You can turn the confirmation and reminder emails on or off under Settings → Email communications → Supervisions & appraisals . Training and supervisions, linked Supervisions are where a manager decides what someone needs, and training is how it gets done. CareStream links the two, so you go into a supervision knowing how the person is doing on their training, and what you agree turns into training that closes itself. The training brief. Before the meeting, open the person from Compliance → Supervisions & appraisals , or open the recording form in your hub, and expand Training brief . It shows what is overdue, due soon or expired, low scores, what they have finished since the last supervision, CQC prep gaps, unanswered questions and open actions, with a short Worth raising list. The training in full. Press See the training in full for a card per course: status, dates, score, time on the lesson, the pre-course check, and every question answered wrongly with their answer and the correct one. With more than one course, each is an accordion that starts closed with a one-line summary, and Open all opens them together. Suggestions, inside each course. Open a course and, at the bottom, you will find ideas for the conversation about that course: for example a low score on a topic, a clear learning gain, a course that is overdue, or all attempts used. Anything that spans more than one course, such as low scores on several, sits in a box at the top. Each suggestion shows the evidence it is based on. They are worked out from the scores and answers by fixed rules, not by AI, so they cost nothing and are the same every time. They are prompts, not judgements, and short courses are worded as “worth checking”. Add as agreed action puts one on the supervision. Allocated training still to do. A closed box near the top lists everything allocated to them that is not finished, of every kind: CPD courses, annual training, ad hoc training and face to face sessions. It is grouped as Missed (past the due date, or a face to face session they did not attend), Part done , Not started , and Not recorded (a face to face session that has passed with no attendance marked, so nobody has said they missed it). A course that has been renewed since, or a missed session made up with the digital catch-up, is not listed. Print or email it. Use Print for a clean page with the CareStream logo, or Send to email to send it to yourself or another administrator on the account. It can only go to an administrator, because it holds a staff member's training records. Allocate training to a supervision. When you assign a course, tick Also add to their next supervision . It adds an action to each person's next booked supervision, and the action closes by itself when they complete the course. Nothing is added unless you tick it, and nothing is created for someone with no supervision booked. A snapshot in the record. When a supervision is completed, a short summary of their training at that time is saved in the record, so it shows what was true on the day. It cannot be edited afterwards. The brief, the training detail and the suggestions are for the supervisor and administrators only. Staff do not see them, but they can see the actions that come out of the supervision in their hub.
