title: Staff incentives
summary: Run a monthly incentive so your team finishes training: points from real records, rewards you choose, and a care manager who approves each one

blocks.title: What it is, on the Professional and Enterprise plans
blocks.text: Staff incentives give your team a reason to keep their training up to date. You set up an incentive for a month. Staff earn points for things CareStream records, and reaching a target unlocks a reward you have chosen, such as a shop voucher or a pizza for the shift. CareStream records, approves and reports. It never buys vouchers or moves money . You give the reward yourself and tell CareStream it has been given. If a reward is paid through pay, or has a cash value, check with your payroll provider or adviser how it should be treated. CareStream does not give tax or employment advice.

blocks.title: 1. Setting up an incentive
blocks.text: Open Incentives in the Team section of the sidebar and click New incentive . Give it a name and choose the month . Points are counted from the first to the last day of that month, and reset each month. Choose who it applies to : everyone, or chosen staff. Agency workers are left out unless you choose them. Add the ways to earn points and how many points each is worth. You can also limit how many times each can count for one person. Add the rewards : a title, an optional picture such as the shop logo, the points needed, and either a number of places or everyone who qualifies. You can add the value of each reward, which the dashboard uses to show what the incentive costs. Optionally set a different target for a person . This keeps it fair for part-time, new and long-serving staff. Click Submit for approval . Use Save draft if you want to come back to it.

blocks.title: 2. How points are earned
blocks.text: Points come only from what CareStream records. Nobody types them in. The ways to earn are: Completes a training module Finishes a module on or before its due date Completes a CPD course Completes an onboarding flow Has a practical sign-off recorded Points follow evidence, never speed. A module only earns points once the assessment has been passed at the module's pass mark. If a module needs an observed practical, it earns nothing until a manager has signed the practical off.

blocks.title: 3. Limited rewards and who wins them
blocks.text: A reward can have a number of places , for example two vouchers this month, or be for everyone who qualifies . When places are limited, they go to the first people to reach the target. “First” is decided by the real time the work was completed, not by when anyone looked at the screen. If two people reached it at exactly the same time and only one place is left, the incentive page flags it and the care manager decides. If a care manager does not approve a reward, or someone leaves, the place passes to the next person in order.

blocks.title: 4. Approvals: the care manager has the final say
blocks.text: A care manager is a staff member whose job role is Care Manager or Registered Manager, usually the person who holds the budget. They approve at two points: The incentive itself , before it goes live. They are emailed when you submit it, and find it under Incentive approvals in their hub. They can approve it or reject it with a reason. Each reward , before it is given. When someone reaches a reward it is held for them, and the care manager approves it. Once approved, someone hands the reward over and clicks Mark as given . Open an incentive and use Download CSV for a list of who has been given what, for payroll or your own records. If you submit an incentive and the home has nobody with the job role Care Manager or Registered Manager, CareStream tells you. Set the job role on the staff record first.

blocks.title: 5. What staff see
blocks.text: My incentives in their hub: their own points, a progress bar for each reward, places left, and how they earned each point. A small live points tracker in the top bar of the hub, on a phone as well as a computer. Emails : one when an incentive starts, a short summary when they earn points (never more than one a day), and at the end of the month a message for the winners and a thank you for everyone else, saying a new incentive will launch soon. Staff see only their own points . There is no leaderboard. If someone misses a limited reward they get a kind thank you that points them to any training still waiting for them, because the aim is a team that keeps its training up to date.

blocks.title: 6. What you see
blocks.text: The Incentives page: every incentive by month, then for each one the rewards, the ways to earn, everyone's progress, and the payouts. The staff record ( Staff , then a person): this month's position and every previous month, award by award. A Staff incentives card on the dashboard : the share of staff who have earned points, rewards reached, waiting and given, the cost this month, and training completions compared with last month. Use Set a monthly budget on the card to see the cost against a budget.

blocks.title: Good to know
blocks.text: An incentive can be renamed at any time. A draft or rejected incentive can also be edited. Once it is live, cancel it and start a new one if you need to change the rules. When someone leaves , they lose access to their points and rewards. A reward already handed over stays on record. When the month ends, the incentive closes and any approved rewards can still be marked as given. There is no dispute process. The results come from what CareStream recorded, and the care manager approves each reward.

title: Agency workers
summary: Time-boxed access, a local induction, and what your agency cover is costing you

blocks.title: Adding an agency worker
blocks.text: Add them from Staff exactly as you would anyone else, then set Staff type to Agency worker . You will be asked for the agency, their first and last day, and optionally a day rate. They then use CareStream like any other member of staff. They can ask the hub questions in their own language, read your policies and complete what you set them. Everything that is different happens around them rather than to them.

blocks.title: Their access ends on its own
blocks.text: The last day you enter is when their access to the hub runs out. You do not have to remember to switch it off. Three days before We email your admins so you can extend the booking or let it end deliberately, rather than finding out afterwards. On the last day Nothing changes. They keep working as normal. 24 hours after Access is withdrawn. The delay is on purpose: a night shift that starts on the last booked day finishes the next morning, and nobody should lose the medication policy at 3am. Nothing is ever deleted. Their training record and completions stay as evidence, whether the booking ends or you archive them.

blocks.title: If they come back, re-book the same person
blocks.text: Agency workers often return. Open their record in Staff and extend the end date rather than adding them again. Adding them a second time creates a second record, and their training history is then split across the two, which is exactly what an inspector will notice.

blocks.title: What is deliberately different
blocks.text: Induction They are enrolled only in the flows you have ticked as suitable for agency, and then only where the job role matches, so an agency nurse gets your nurse induction and nothing else. Use the Add for Agency Staff button on a flow on the Onboarding page. Most homes tick the inductions they already run for care assistants and nurses rather than building separate ones. Compliance They do not appear on the compliance register. Their DBS, right to work and professional registration are held by the agency, not by you, so chasing you for paperwork you cannot hold would leave the register permanently red. Supervisions They are not listed for supervisions or appraisals, so they never show as overdue for something nobody intends to book. Your plan Agency workers do not use one of your staff places. They are covering a gap, not filling a post. You still need evidence that the agency has done those checks. Keep their assurance with your agency paperwork; CareStream is not claiming to hold it for you.

blocks.title: What agency cover is costing you
blocks.text: Because every booking has dates, CareStream can total how many agency days you have used, broken down by agency. Add a day rate when you book someone and it will cost that up for you too. Leave the rate blank and you still get the days. The totals appear on the Staff page, in the Agency spend panel above your staff list, whenever you have agency bookings. Most homes know agency is expensive but cannot say how expensive without going back through invoices. This is that number, without the digging.

title: Named role holders & changing a name
summary: How your policies know who your Medicines Lead is, and what happens when that person changes

blocks.title: Where the names come from
blocks.text: Settings › Organisation details lists the roles a care policy names a person against: Registered manager, Medicines lead, Data protection officer, Deputy manager and so on. Each role can hold more than one person. Names reach a role two ways. A chip marked STAFF comes from a staff member's job role or specialism on their record, so it has no remove button here: change it on their record in Staff . A plain chip is one you typed, and can be removed with the × beside it.

blocks.title: Most policies update themselves
blocks.text: Your policies are written to name the role , and the current holder's name is added when the policy is displayed. So a policy saying “the Medicines Lead checks the controlled drugs register” shows as “the Medicines Lead (Priya Shah)” wherever it is read: preview, review, download and the staff hub. Change the name in Settings and those policies show the new one immediately. Nothing is rewritten, no new version is created, and there is nothing to approve, because the policy itself never changed.

blocks.title: Some policies have the name written in
blocks.text: A policy we write for you names the person once, at the point their role first takes a responsibility. A policy you uploaded may name somebody directly without using the role title at all. In both cases the name is part of the text and will not update on its own. So when you remove a named person, CareStream checks your policies first. If any of them have that name written in, you are shown which policies, how many mentions, and the wording around each one before anything changes. You then choose: Update the policies Replaces the name throughout each policy and saves a new version of each. Every mention moves, not just the first. Remove only Takes the person off the role but leaves your policies exactly as they are. Use this when nobody has taken the role on yet.

blocks.title: What gets recorded
blocks.text: Each updated policy gets a new point version (2.0 becomes 2.1) and an entry in Policies › History showing the role, the old name, the new name and the date. Staff see the corrected wording straight away, and so does the AI when answering questions. A name change does not go through manager or external approval. Correcting who holds a role is not a change to what the policy requires, in the same way that fixing a typo is not. The check reads every one of your policies , not just the ones we hold as editable text. Where a policy names the person but CareStream has no working copy of it yet, you are told so plainly rather than left to assume nothing was found. Those keep the old name until the policy is adopted through Policy Gap Detection. Removing a person from a role does not archive them from Staff : if they have also left, archive them there separately.

title: AI tokens & your monthly allowance
summary: What tokens are, how many your plan includes, what uses them, and when they reset

blocks.title: What a token is, in plain terms
blocks.text: Every time CareStream asks its AI to do something, the work is measured in tokens . A token is roughly three quarters of a word, counting both what we send the AI (your policy text, the question) and what it sends back. Writing a training module is tens of thousands of tokens; analysing your whole policy library against the regulations is a few million. You do not need to think in tokens day to day. The number exists so you can see what you have used and what is left, in the same way you would look at a mobile data allowance.

blocks.title: What your plan includes
blocks.text: Plan AI tokens each month Roughly enough for Starter 6 million A full policy gap analysis plus a handful of tailored training modules Professional 18 million Regular gap analysis across a larger library, with training generation through the month Enterprise 30 million Heavy use across multiple services To put that in context: a busy 40-bed home running gap analysis and generating training through the month typically uses around a quarter of the Enterprise allowance.

blocks.title: What uses tokens, and what does not
blocks.text: Uses your allowance Policy gap analysis — regulation coverage, out-of-date content, cross-policy consistency and CQC wording. This is the biggest user by some distance. Tailoring training to your policies, and generating cover images. Generating CQC prep questions , audit recommendations and onboarding questions. Translating content into a staff member's own language. Does not touch your allowance Questions your staff ask in the hub. These have their own separate monthly limit, shown beside your tokens on the dashboard. Running out of tokens never stops a carer getting an answer on shift. Assigning standard training modules from the CareStream library. Those are already written, so they are free. Resuming an interrupted analysis. Anything already analysed is not done twice.

blocks.title: Seeing where you are
blocks.text: Open your Dashboard . The AI tokens card shows what you have used against your allowance, with a bar that turns amber past 70% and red past 90%. On any AI feature page, the same figure appears as a line at the top, so you know where you stand before starting something large. The card also shows the reset date.

blocks.title: When it resets, and what happens if you run out
blocks.text: Your allowance resets on the 1st of each month , whatever date you joined on. It does not roll over: an unused allowance does not carry into next month, so there is nothing to be gained by holding back. If you use it all, AI generation pauses until the 1st. Everything else carries on as normal — your staff keep asking questions, your policies stay available, training already assigned still runs, and nothing is lost. You will see a message telling you the allowance is spent. If you need more before the reset, moving up a plan increases the allowance immediately. If you are close to the limit and have a large job to run, such as a full gap analysis, it is worth waiting for the reset rather than starting something that stops part way.

blocks.title: Why tokens rather than a number of actions
blocks.text: We used to count actions , which sounds simpler but is not fair: analysing a 90-page policy and generating one training question both counted as one, despite being wildly different amounts of work. Tokens measure the actual work, so a small job costs a small amount and you are not charged the same for both.

text: What a token is, in plain terms Every time CareStream asks its AI to do something, the work is measured in tokens . A token is roughly three quarters of a word, counting both what we send the AI (your policy text, the question) and what it sends back. Writing a training module is tens of thousands of tokens; analysing your whole policy library against the regulations is a few million. You do not need to think in tokens day to day. The number exists so you can see what you have used and what is left, in the same way you would look at a mobile data allowance. What your plan includes Plan AI tokens each month Roughly enough for Starter 6 million A full policy gap analysis plus a handful of tailored training modules Professional 18 million Regular gap analysis across a larger library, with training generation through the month Enterprise 30 million Heavy use across multiple services To put that in context: a busy 40-bed home running gap analysis and generating training through the month typically uses around a quarter of the Enterprise allowance. What uses tokens, and what does not Uses your allowance Policy gap analysis — regulation coverage, out-of-date content, cross-policy consistency and CQC wording. This is the biggest user by some distance. Tailoring training to your policies, and generating cover images. Generating CQC prep questions , audit recommendations and onboarding questions. Translating content into a staff member's own language. Does not touch your allowance Questions your staff ask in the hub. These have their own separate monthly limit, shown beside your tokens on the dashboard. Running out of tokens never stops a carer getting an answer on shift. Assigning standard training modules from the CareStream library. Those are already written, so they are free. Resuming an interrupted analysis. Anything already analysed is not done twice. Seeing where you are Open your Dashboard . The AI tokens card shows what you have used against your allowance, with a bar that turns amber past 70% and red past 90%. On any AI feature page, the same figure appears as a line at the top, so you know where you stand before starting something large. The card also shows the reset date. When it resets, and what happens if you run out Your allowance resets on the 1st of each month , whatever date you joined on. It does not roll over: an unused allowance does not carry into next month, so there is nothing to be gained by holding back. If you use it all, AI generation pauses until the 1st. Everything else carries on as normal — your staff keep asking questions, your policies stay available, training already assigned still runs, and nothing is lost. You will see a message telling you the allowance is spent. If you need more before the reset, moving up a plan increases the allowance immediately. If you are close to the limit and have a large job to run, such as a full gap analysis, it is worth waiting for the reset rather than starting something that stops part way. Why tokens rather than a number of actions We used to count actions , which sounds simpler but is not fair: analysing a 90-page policy and generating one training question both counted as one, despite being wildly different amounts of work. Tokens measure the actual work, so a small job costs a small amount and you are not charged the same for both.

title: Plans, billing & closing your account
summary: Upgrade your plan, manage billing, and how to delete your account

blocks.title: Your plan & upgrading
blocks.text: Your current plan, monthly price, and annual training allocation are shown on the Dashboard and on the Billing page. Each plan includes a monthly pool of annual training allocations (Starter 10, Professional 30, Enterprise unlimited) — one allocation is one annual training module assigned to one staff member. Go to Billing in the sidebar (or click Upgrade plan on the Dashboard). Under Upgrade your plan , the higher tiers available to you are listed with their features and price. Click Upgrade to … to go to secure Stripe checkout. Upgrades take effect immediately and unlock the new features straight away. Locked features (for example Face-to-face training, Build your own audit, Supervisions and appraisals with training linked to them, or the Effectiveness and Training Impact reports) show an Upgrade prompt that takes you to Billing. Your existing data is always kept exactly as it is when you change plan.

blocks.title: Managing payment & invoices
blocks.text: Use Manage billing on the Billing page to open the secure Stripe portal, where you can update your card, change payment details, and download invoices. Your invoice history is also listed on the Billing page. CareStream never sees or stores your card details.

blocks.title: Deleting your account
blocks.text: If you need to close your account, you can do it yourself from Settings → Danger zone → Delete account . This is a serious, account-wide action, so it asks you to confirm by typing DELETE . When you delete your account, we immediately: Cancel your subscription so you are not billed again. Sign out and deactivate every login on the account, so no one (admins or staff) can sign in. Queue all of your data (policies, staff, training, audits) for permanent erasure. Changed your mind? Our team can restore a closed account for 30 days . After that, the data is permanently erased and cannot be recovered. To restore, contact support before the 30 days are up. Only an admin can delete the account. If you only want to stop being billed but keep your data, use Manage billing to cancel your subscription instead of deleting the account.
